articleTitle: Monopole Antenna with Frequency Selective Surface for Microwave Breast Cancer Detection
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This work introduces a monopole antenna based on metamaterials for breast cancer identification. The put forward antenna is built on an FR4 substrate with a dielectric constant of 4.4, loss tangent 0.025 and thickness of 1.6 mm. For gain enhancement, the designed antenna is equipped with a frequency selective surface (FSS) on its back side. The suggested antenna obtains a broad bandwidth (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> > 10 dB) between 2.3 and 22.3 GHz, with a apex gain of 9.3 dBi at 12 GHz. The put forward work also achieves a maximum gain enhancement of 5 dBi with the addition of FSS at the back side of the antenna. The Specific absorption Rate (SAR) study of the antenna with a realistic homogeneous breast phantom modelled in the simulator is performed to assess the effect of radiation on the breast. It is observed that the suggested antenna agrees with the International limits when averaged over 1g of tissue.

articleTitle: Preliminary Feed Assembly Design for INCUS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a preliminary feed assembly design for a new Earth science mission to be flown on a small satellite platform, recently approved by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA). The feed consists of a cluster of seven identical feedhorns at Ka-band fed by WR28 waveguides. Detailed RF and mechanical models are presented for both the feedhorns and the feeding waveguide runs. RF performance, including gain, insertion loss and coupling between feeds will also be discussed. Finally, details about the proposed preliminary fabrication approach will be provided, including a prototype single horn recently fabricated at the Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL).

articleTitle: Octuple Ridge Conical Horn Antenna with Hemispherical Dielectric Lens Loading for Biomedical Imaging Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The proposed work depicts a compact Octuple Ridge Conical Horn (ORCH) antenna that can be utilized for Microwave Imaging (MI). The put forward ORCH is appended with a hemispherical dielectric lens to improve its gain and radiation properties. The proposed antenna achieves a bandwidth from 3 - 20 GHz with good return loss performance. The designed antenna obtains a maximum realized gain of 27.85 dBi at 20 GHz . The usage of the ORCH for MI applications is tested by checking its Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) readings in the Computer Simulation Technology (CST) simulation software. It is found that the SAR value complies with the international regulations.

articleTitle: A Conformal, Planar Inverted F Antenna using Low-Cost Multilayer PET sheet for Vehicular Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A planar inverted F antenna (PIFA) has been designed using low-cost PET sheets for vehicular application. Energy dispersive X-ray (EDX) and microstrip ring resonator method is used for material characterization of PET sheets. The dielectric properties of PET sheet are found to be є<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> =2.63 and tanδ =0.004 respectively. The planar PIFA antenna was designed and analyzed using ANSYSS HFSS software. It is evident from the analysis that the PIFA works at its fundamental mode (TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">10</inf>) for desired frequency band. The proposed antenna is fabricated and tested in planar as well conformal conditions. A good match has been observed between the simulated and the measured results. The measured realized gain of the PIFA antenna on planar and conformal conditions was nearly same (≈ 6.0 dBi). As per the literature survey, it is evident that this is the first attempt to use the reported methodology for conformal PIFA design on PET sheets for vehicular application.

Author Keywords: Planar inverted F antenna (PIFA Polyethylene terephthalate (PET))

articleTitle: Uncertainty Quantification Analysis for a Ka-band Deployable Mesh Reflector for INCUS
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a statistical analysis to evaluate the impact of fabrication tolerances of a deployable mesh reflector on its electromagnetic performance. This study is carried out assigning a random displacement of the nodes composing the mesh of the reflector from their ideal position along the parabolic shape. This analysis is applied to a deployable mesh reflector operating at Ka-band which is being considered for a new NASA Earth science mission. The goal of this study is to evaluate how much an incorrect placement of the nodes will impact the radiation pattern of the reflector and its pointing.

articleTitle: Ultra broadband 1-6GHz and 6-10GHz Bandpass Filters for Frequency Multiplexer
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper demonstrates the initial stage of developing a 1-18GHz five port frequency multiplexer. The design details of 1-6GHz and 6-10GHz bandpass filters are discussed along with their results. Modified optimum short-circuited stub technique is used for designing a 1-6GHz bandpass filter, and cascading high pass filter with low pass filter is used for the design of a 6-10GHz bandpass filter. Both filters achieve a passband return loss <-15dB, passband insertion loss <2dB and stopband attenuation > 50 dB.

articleTitle: Rectangular Patch Antenna with Truncated Cuts and Slot for Satellite Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A rectangular patch antenna with truncated cuts and a slot in the center of the rectangular patch suitable for satellite communication applications is proposed in this paper. The dimensions of the proposed antenna is 18.5 × 21.8 × 1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and the dimensions of the patch is 8.9 × 12.2 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The proposed antenna is a triple band antenna, resonating at 3.6GHz, 6.7GHz, and 14.1GHz with a bandwidth of 530MHz (3.42GHz to 3.95GHz), 990MHz (6.50GHz to 7.49GHz) and 3.67GHz (13.05GHz to 16.72GHz) with a gain of 1.67 dBi, 5.91 dBi, and 5.30 dBi respectively. By incorporating an L-Shaped DGS offers a circular polarization band of 260MHz (16.21GHz to 16.47GHz) is obtained. The proposed antenna operates in S, C and Ku bands useful for satellite communication applications. Simulations are carried out using Ansys HFSS software.

articleTitle: Comparative Study of Chipless RFID Tag Resonator for Orientation-Independent Properties and Bit-Capacity
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Radio frequency identification (RFID) is a growing technology in various domains for identification and tracking purposes. Wearable and on-body sensing technology are significant topics in the industrial, scientific, and medical fields. Based on the presence of the IC chip, RFID tags can be classified into chipped and chipless tags. Recently, chipless RFID tags are being investigated because of their high usage and low cost. Orientation-independent chipless RFID tags are promising for future wearable sensing devices. Therefore, an understanding of the orientation-independent Chipless RFID tags is necessary to develop the sensor tags. The paper’s main purpose is to explore the flexibility of the chipless RFID tag for rotation insensitivity and coding capacity. Here, conventional shapes of resonators like square, circle, triangle and hexagon in microstrip patch configuration are studied for the orientation-independent property. Further, concentric circular ring and slot configurations are discussed for high bit-capacity.

articleTitle: Modified plus-Shaped Microstrip Patch Antenna with DGS for Ultra Wide-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a modified plus-shaped patch antenna with Defected Ground Structure (DGS) is presented for ultra-wideband applications. The proposed antenna dimensions are 38x48x1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. In this, a square patch antenna is modified by incorporating a modified plus-shaped slot and truncated cuts resulting in a triple band offering a bandwidth of 1.11GHz (6.45GHz-7.55GHz), 210MHz(10.28GHz-10.50GHz)and 1.10GHz (13.51GHz-14.61GHz).By incorporating DGS the ultra-wideband is achieved with the bandwidth of 8.85GHz (6.39 GHz-14.73GHz) and the peak gain obtained 3.79dBi at 7.1GHz and 5.75dBi at 12.8GHz. The VSWR is ≤ 2 across the full UWB range. A high-frequency structure simulator (HFSS) is used to analyze this antenna's performance.

articleTitle: LoRa-based Novel System for Smart Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Smart agriculture is a growing field that uses advanced technology to improve the efficiency, productivity, and sustainability of farming operations. One of the key technologies used in smart agriculture is Low Power Wide Area Network (LPWAN). A LPWAN protocol enables long-range wireless communication between IoT sensors and devices. In this paper, we propose a LoRa based smart agriculture management system that uses LPWAN technology to monitor and control various aspects of agriculture operations. The system consists of wireless sensors and devices deployed in the field to collect data on soil moisture levels, crop growth, weather conditions, and other factors that impact agriculture operations. The collected data is then transmitted to a central management system for analysis and decision-making. The system is designed to optimize irrigation, crop management, and other agricultural practices leading to increased efficiency, productivity, and sustainability. For the proposed system a microstrip patch antenna operating at 868 MHz is designed and developed. Performance of the proposed system is tested and validated by using developed antennas. The proposed system has the potential to revolutionize the way agriculture is managed, by enabling farmers to make data-driven decisions and respond quickly to changes in environmental conditions.

articleTitle: Design of a PlanarInverted-F Antenna (PIFA) 2.4 GHz for Bluetooth and WLAN applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Bluetooth and WLAN services are playing an important role nowadays in wireless communications. For these applications, a novel PIFA (Planar Inverted-F Antenna) design is described. The proposed design employs a single feed port and shorting plate in its geometry. Bandwidth achieved by the design is 335 MHz (2.15 GHz to 2.49 GHz at -10 dB base line). The peak gain achieved by this design is 4.74 dB. Gain of antenna without shorting plate is 1.5 dB, which being significantly lesser than the design with 4mm wide shorting plate gain. Use of shorting plate provides improved bandwidth and gain values. Comparisons are drawn with other PIFA antennas based on performance measures. The antenna is suitable for Bluetooth and WLAN usage owing to its bandwidth and other integral parameters. The design produces a higher gain and a low VSWR value providing a performance advantage.

articleTitle: Design of An Ultrawideband Antenna with triple notch band characteristics
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)

authors.preferredName: B. S. S. V. Ramesh Babu

abstract: In present scenario, we are surrounded with multiple communication devices with multiple frequency of operation. Thus, the various frequency bands may produce interference with desired band of operation. The works proposes an ultra-wide band antenna with operation range of 3.1GHz-10.6GHz and has triple notch band rejection frequencies of 4.2 GHz −4.6GHz, 6.6 GHz −7.6 GHz, and 9.0 GHz – 9.3 GHz to reduce in interference within the notch band frequencies. The proposed antenna has a gain of 4 dBi in its operational range and very low gain in notch band frequencies.

articleTitle: Design of a MIMO Rectangular Dielectric Resonator Antenna for 5G Millimeter-Wave Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This works describes the design of a highly isolated wideband two-element semi-circular shaped patch with rectangular dielectric resonator antenna (RDRA). The antenna is operated at (24GHz - 40 GHz) that covers Ka-band (27 GHz -40GHz). Dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) is positioned perpendicular to one another in order to accomplish the desired wide-band functioning with good impedance matching, increased gain, and bandwidth. To improve the isolation between antenna elements, diamond shape slot is etched in the ground plane. The DRA configuration provides a higher gain of approximately 7.8 dB and nearly omnidirectional radiation patterns. In addition, the recommended DRA MIMO performance parameters are examined and reported. The results indicate that the suggested DRA MIMO antenna is considered a suitable contender for 5G millimeter wave-based applications.

articleTitle: Moore Curve Fractal-Shaped Frequency Selective Surface for Multiband Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this work Fractal based Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) is presented. Fractals are self-repetitive geometries that can provide a multiband operation. FSS unit cell designed using Moore curve fractals up to the third iteration and analyzed in terms of return loss and transmission coefficient. The FSS is designed over a Fr-4 substrate with a thickness of 1.6 mm. The Moore Curve shaped frequency Selective Surface (MCFSS) iteration 1 has a single-band operation at 8.56 GHz while MCFSS iteration 2 has dual-band operation at 4.3GHz and 8.59 GHz, and MCFSS iteration three has dual-band response at 2.36 GHz and 4.89 GHz.

articleTitle: Analysis of Feed Network Efficiency in Time-Modulated Linear and Circular Array
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, the feed network analysis and directivity have been addressed using time-modulated linear and circular antenna arrays. 16-Element linear and circular antennas are considered for calculating feed network efficiency and directivity using CRPSO (Craziness-based Particle Swarm Optimization). An optimal combination of switch-ON time sequences provides an array pattern with feed network efficiency and directivity using this technique. Simulations are done in MATLAB. The results are shown in the numerical result section.

articleTitle: Series fed Circular patch Antenna 3x1 array for C Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents an array of series coaxial feeding microstrip antennae with three circular patch elements at resonant frequency 5.8 GHz for the ISM band having a return loss (S11) of -14.95 dB. The designed antenna has a property of radiation pattern having directive gain 3.21dB and BW is 210 MHz ANSYS electromagnetics suite and HFSS are used to simulate the proposed antenna's gain, radiation pattern, return loss, and parametric optimizations. The proposed circular microstrip antenna array is aimed to use for C-band wideband applications like monitoring of weather (climate), medical, and ATC, to regulate traffic on maritime vessels, defense monitoring, and detection of the velocity of vehicles for law enforcement.

articleTitle: Circular Ring Fractal UWB Antenna for Microwave Imaging Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this work, an ultra-wideband (UWB) planar antenna design is presented that is suitable for microwave imaging applications. The radiating element is comprised of three connected rings connected through thin metallic strips that correspond to fractal geometry. The antenna’s bottom side utilizes a stair-shaped slot-based partial ground plane to achieve UWB response. The use of a stair-shaped slot also helps in achieving good impedance matching in the UWB frequency range. The proposed antenna design exhibits a total dimension of 18×20 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. An impedance bandwidth of ≈31.68 GHz is observed within the frequency range of 3.32 GHz ≈ to beyond 35 GHz. Furthermore, the proposed UWB antenna shows a fractional bandwidth (FBW) of 165.35% and a peak gain of ≈8.5 dBi within the desired operating range. It is evident from the results that the proposed antenna exhibits exceptional low-dispersive characteristics across a broad frequency spectrum, which makes it highly suitable for microwave imaging applications.

articleTitle: Generation of a Dual-Mode OAM Beam using a CP UCA Antenna for Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a multilayer uniform circular array (UCA) with circularly polarized (CP) patch elements is proposed to generates dual-mode orbital angular momentum (OAM) beams. To eliminate the dependency of phase excitation on feed length, the proposed UCA is designed with a CP elliptical patch as an array of elements that are geometrically rotated to obtain the desired phase excitation. By providing the input excitation of the feed network strategically, the resultant CP radiating patches can be excited for generating OAM modes l = +1 or +2 respectively. The UCA’s performance is determined in terms of S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>, radiation pattern, and $\vec E$-field phase distribution. According to the simulation results, the UCA produces a dual-mode OAM beam at 5.9 GHz. Therefore, the proposed UCA could be advantageous for wireless communication systems.

articleTitle: A Compact Planar Semi-Elliptical Antenna for UWB Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a compact semi-elliptical monopole structure with Asymmetric Coplanar Strip (ACS) feeding having Ultra-Wide Band (UWB) characteristics. The proposed semi-elliptical patch radiator is having a size of 5.5×4.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and is fed by 50-ohm impedance ACS line of dimensions 3.058×8.22 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and is printed on an FR4 Epoxy substrate of size 28 × 11.5 × 1.6 mm.<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> A sectorial bending its created on coplanar ground plane to get the desirable UWB characteristics. The antenna is fabricated and tested for the performance. The measured impedance bandwidth covers entire UWB range with good return loss characteristics. This antenna Would be promising for high-speed communication.

articleTitle: Lumped-Element Based Tunable Bandstop Filter for Airborne UHF Communication System
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Airborne tactical communication systems are facing a significant issue with RF co-site interference caused by various factors such as jamming, nearby radio stations, or co-located RF systems on the same aircraft. This interference can cause the receiver's front-end amplifier to compress and distort, which can mask weaker signals of interest. The frequency of interferer signals can also vary over time, making it challenging to address the problem. However, the paper presents a potential solution in the form of a tunable lumped-element based band-stop filter for UHF-band radio systems. The filter's tunable range spans from 225 MHz to 400 MHz and can provide a rejection bandwidth of 2.5 MHz to 4 MHz, which can be controlled by adjusting the scaling capacitor and resonant capacitor values. This proposed topology offers greater flexibility in terms of frequency and bandwidth control, making it more adaptable to changing interference frequencies over time. Overall, this paper presents a promising solution to the issue of RF co-site interference faced by airborne tactical communication systems.

articleTitle: Polarization Switching Frequency Reconfigurable Dual Polarization Antenna Element for Phased Array Weather Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, design of a C-band frequency reconfigurable and polarization switching aperture coupled microstrip antenna is proposed. This antenna operates at two distinct frequencies and switches between horizontal and vertical polarizations and can be used in a phased array antenna. The antenna is an aperture-coupled microstrip element designed to switch between frequency range of 4.72 to 4.90 GHz and 5.27 to 5.41 GHz with a gain of 4.7-5.5 dB for all polarizations and frequencies of interest. The polarization switching is achieved by using a switch at the feedlines. Frequency reconfigurability is achieved using diodes to change the effective size of the patch. The simulations show that the antenna is able to alternate between the two polarizations using a switch on the feedlines at two frequency bands with a cross-polarization level of more than 30 dB.

articleTitle: An X-band U-Slot Modified Square Microstrip Patch Antenna with wide beam and high gain for Radar applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, an antenna element feasible for phased array antenna (PAA) systems is proposed. The design methodology for a PAA element is presented in the form of a flow diagram. The design procedure of a U-Slot Modified Square Microstrip Patch Antenna (USMSMPA) operating in the X-band is presented through simulations. The designed antenna element is then gauged based on Mutual Coupling (MC) and Scanning Capability in a 7 × 7 array environment. A 7 × 7 array of the USMSMPA is constructed and it’s properties are analyzed using Finite Array Domain Decomposition Method(FADDM) in HFSS. The scan volume of the array is determined by observing the drop in gain for subsequent increase in the steering angle. The 7 × 7 array of the antenna element achieves a scan volume of more than ±55°. The coupling in all variations of the 7 × 7 array is < -20 dB showing a maximum value of -19 dB.

articleTitle: Optimised Direction of Arrival Estimation for Shaped Dielectric Lens Antennas using Curve Fitting Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In traditional DOA estimation algorithms, the refractive and curvature effects of the lens antenna are not considered and the estimated arrival angle is Virtual Direction of Arrival (VDOA). DOA algorithms considering the lens effects compute Actual Direction of arrival (ADOA) but they are computationally exhaustive and needs abundant memory. In this paper ADOA is efficiently computed and ADOA-VDOA relationship is established by Curve Fitting Method (CFM). In CFM the relation between ADOA and VDOA is developed using the Ray Tracing approach. This relation is approximated and fits into a cubic polynomial, this polynomial is a function of the dielectric constant, the curvature of shaped lens and VDOA. This analysis is carried out for a hemispherical lens - linear array antenna. The CFM method is compared with the traditional Ray Tracing procedure and found to be in close agreement.

articleTitle: Design and development of smooth wall spline profiled horn antenna for SATCOM application at Ku band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a design of high gain smooth wall spline profiled horn antenna is discussed and developed for Ku band frequency range of 10.7GHz-11.45GHz for transmit (Tx) and 12.75GHz-13.25GHz for receive (Rx) band of communication satellite at geostationary orbit. The detailed design procedure is discussed for achieving required edge of coverage gain. The horn is designed, simulated, fabricated and integrated with slot coupled orthomode transducer (OMT) for dual linear polarization applications. The RF characterizations of the feed chain has been carried out, in which the return loss better than 19dB as well as port-to-port isolation better than 40dB of the OMT is obtained in the measurement; moreover pattern measurement is also performed in anechoic chamber. The edge of coverage (2.67<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> half-cone angle) gain better than 24dBi and cross-pol better than 30dB within the coverage region is obtained in the measurement.

articleTitle: A Circular Patch with Rectangular-Slotted Ground Super-Wideband Two-Port MIMO Antenna for Multiple Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This research article analyses a super-wideband monopole two-port MIMO antenna which radiates electromagnetic energy efficiently. The proposed antenna is designed as a single-port on dielectric material occupying the space of 10×12 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with a circular patch printed on the top plane of the substrate and rectangular-slotted ground on the opposite side of the substrate which has a dielectric constant value of 2.20 with thickness 0.254mm. This antenna offers a bandwidth of 8.51GHz-51.74GHz with two deep resonances at 10.40GHz and 40.40GHz. This antenna also offers an average peak realized gain and directivity of 5.09dBi and 6.20dBi. The two-port MIMO version of the single-port is transformed by placing two identical-circular patches adjacent to each other with an edge-to-edge spacing of 7.50mm to maintain the bandwidth of 8.00GHz-50.0GHz. The inter-spacing achieves isolation of more than 14.80dB with average diversity parameter Envelope Correlation Coefficient42.0GHz=0.011, Diversity Gain42.0GHz=9.764dB, Total Active Reflection Coeffieicnt42.0GHz=-38.0dB, and Channel Capacity Loss42.0GHz=0.102b/s/Hz in the 40GHz bandwidth. The proposed MIMO antenna is a probable candidate for multiple wireless applications including X-Band RADAR, Ku-Band Satellite System, and millimeter-Wave 5G Technology bands FR2 ranging between 24.0GHz-40.0GHz and can be deployed in mobile wireless infrastructure in the electromagnetic Wave environment.

articleTitle: Design of Bow-tie Antenna over High Impedance Surface for Bluetooth and WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This work proposes a bow-tie antenna for wearable Bluetooth applications designed over a square-ring High Impedance Surface (HIS). HIS structures have the advantage of surface wave reduction and zero-phase reflection of radiation. These properties are much required for wearable antennas. In this work, square-shaped HIS cell is studied for via and via less in terms of its reflection phase characteristics. The proposed bow-tie antenna over square-ring HIS 6 × 6 array provides a wide bandwidth of 1.8 GHz with a frequency range of 4.43 GHz–6.31 GHz with a maximum return loss of -28.9 dBi with a peak gain of 3.7 dBi.

articleTitle: A Novel 5th order high selective filtering isolator with static and time-modulated resonators
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a novel lumped element 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> order non-reciprocal bandpass filter is presented with improved selectivity. This filter combines outer time-invariant and inner time-modulated resonators to generate a non-reciprocal filering isolation using the concept of spatio-temporal modulation. Off late, this concept has grabbed attention, where the typical operation relies on the time-modulation of space separated resonators using sinusoidal signals with an incremental phase shift. The simulated results reveal a nonreciprocal response within the passband bandwith with a steep selectivity owing to the higher order of the filter. This configuration paves the pathway for the design of various higher order filtering isolators.

articleTitle: Mushroom Unit Cell Loaded Triple Band Microstrip Antenna for Sub-6 GHz MIMO and Phased Array Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a mushroom unit-cell loaded mult-iband microstrip antenna sub-array is proposed. Here, the mushroom unit-cell surrounded with a square slot is etched out at the diagonal corner of the square patch antenna to achieve multi-band response (3.21 GHz, 3.42 GHz, 3.68 GHz) at sub-6 GHz frequency band. The proposed technique achieves antenna miniaturization yielding a footprint of 0.19λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.19λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the free space wavelength at 3. 21 GHz. Next, the proposed antenna is used to con figure 2 × 2 sub-array for MIMO / phased array applications. The proposed sub-array achieves satisfactory impedance matching of ≤ −15 dB, interport isolation of ≤ 25 dB, better SLL of ≤ −20 dB, maximum sub-array gain of 7.6 dBi, and 3 dB beam width of 59<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>. Further, the proposed 2 × 2 sub-array demonstrates beam steering up to 80<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup>. The proposed sub-array is fabricated and validated by s-parameter measurement.

articleTitle: Button Sized Wearable Antenna Design for ISM Frequency Bands
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A button-shaped wearable antenna is presented for Industrial Scientific Medical (ISM) frequency bands. This is incorporated by two radiating patches on both sides of the button shaped Rogers 5880 dielectric substrate. It is situated on the top of a cotton textile substrate and a conductive textile below this textile is used as ground. The simulation is done in FIT based CST studio suite software without and with a human phantom wrist for analyzing the antenna characteristics. It shows distinct radiation patterns for the ISM frequency bands, i.e. at 2.4 GHz band and at 5.4 GHz band. Two operating bands are observed from 2.41 GHz to 2.49 GHz and from 5.2 GHz to 5.7 GHz. Radiation patterns and surface currents at the desired frequencies are studied. The analyzed Specific Absorption Rate (SAR) values are satisfactory and within limits for medical applications.

articleTitle: Reconfigurable Wideband Monopole Radiator using Paper Substrate for Bluetooth/ISM Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Reconfigurable antennas are required to be upgraded with the extensive utilisation for wireless and Internet of Things (IoT) applications. This works deals with compact and cost-effective antenna design that operates in multiple frequencies by the use of switching circuits. These switching circuits are the PIN diodes connected between the main radiator, the inverse L-shaped radiator and a U-shaped radiator. The four switching states of PIN diodes i.e., "ON-ON", "ON-OFF", "OFF-ON" and "OFF-OFF" connect and disconnect the radiators to provide multi-band frequencies. The non-radiating capacitive element of 10pF is used between the microstrip-line and the main radiator for frequency tuning. The antenna is designed on low-cost paper substrate that makes it inexpensive for production and covers an overall area of 43mm x 40mm x 0.44mm. The antenna efficiently work for bluetooth services, 5G mobile band and ISM band over a frequency range of 1.6GHz to 3.5GHz. The antenna gain and efficiency are 1.1 and more than 80% in the desire band respectively. All the simulated results such as reflection coefficient, gain, radiation pattern and efficiency proves the antenna to be in a favourable concurrence.

articleTitle: A Wideband Fabry Perot Cavity Antenna-based Feed Cluster for Multibeam Space Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper proposes a new design of a Fabry Perot Cavity Antenna (FPCA) based Feed Cluster with seven feed elements in the S-band. A dual-layer Partially Reflective Screen (PRS) based design was incorporated in order to meet a broad bandwidth requirement uncharacteristic of conventional FPCA clusters. The cluster has been realized with an extremely small feed-to-feed spacing of 1λ for a specific Multibeam Antenna application which requires high edge taper values for the radiation patterns of feed elements. The mutual coupling has been managed by using matched filters to maintain the quality of radiation patterns despite the high reflectivity PRS structure and close packing of feeds. An edge taper better than -14 dB has been attained for all feed elements at the specified angles. A bandwidth requirement of 9.6% from 2.5 to 2.75 GHz has been effectively met.

articleTitle: Hexagonal Hybrid DRA Circularly Polarized Antenna for Multiband Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this work, a hybrid structure containing a hexagonal microstrip patch antenna with hexagonal rings loaded with a Dielectric Resonator (DR) is presented. The length of the hexagonal patch and DR is 10 mm. The height of Al2O3 ceramic DR is 7mm with an overall dimension of the proposed antenna of 51x45x1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The proposed antenna operates over multiple frequency ranges resulting in bandwidths of 30MHz (4.38–4.41 GHz), 230MHz (6.99-7.22 GHz), 100MHz (7.84–7.94 GHz), 650MHz (9.82–10.47 GHz), 110MHz (11.31–11.42 GHz), 70MHz (12.04–12.11 GHz), 340MHz (12.33-12.67 GHz) and 150MHz (13.03–13.18 GHz). The peak gain of the antenna is observed to be 6.61 dBi at 10.28 GHz and circular polarization characteristics are observed over the multiple frequencies ranges with a bandwidth of 210MHz (6.73-6.94 GHz), 100MHz (7.22-7.32 GHz), 90MHz (9.16-9.25 GHz), 140MHz (9.67-9.81 GHz), and 130MHz (11.42-11.55 GHz). Using bent microstrip line feed, two orthogonal modes are created resulting in CP radiation. The proposed antenna is suitable for C, X, and Ku band applications. The simulations are carried out using HFSS software.

articleTitle: Development of stepped microstrip fed Triangular-slot DGS antenna for UWB Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A stepped microstrip fed, triangular slotted defected ground structure is suggested in the paper for ultra-wideband (UWB) applications. An FR4 substrate sized 34 mm x 38 mm with a thickness of 1.6 mm is used for prototyping the antenna. A tapered radiating patch is proposed with triangular-shaped structures on the top edges. Due to the design of a triangular-shaped defected ground structure (DGS), the antenna is tuned from 2.68 GHz to 10.39 GHz. The detailed step analysis is discussed in this paper. For the entire operating range, the peak gain is between 0.5 dBi to 4.5 dBi, and radiation efficiency ranges between 80 % and 90 %. The simulated results show that the designed antenna is well-suited for ultra-wideband wireless systems.

articleTitle: High Gain Cylindrical Cavity-Backed Crossed Dipole Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A circularly polarized (CP) crossed dipole antenna backed with Perfect Electric Conductor (PEC) and cylindrical cavity reflectors are presented in this paper. The performance of these reflectors is compared here. A comparative study of CP antenna features on PEC and Cavity-backed reflectors to that of reference antenna is carried out in this work. The crossed dipole backed by a cylindrical cavity is able to achieve unidirectional radiation pattern, high gain, high front-to-back ratio along with an efficiency > 90%. The 0.26 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.23 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> (where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is free space wavelength at 1.58 GHz) sized antenna backed by a cavity structure yields a total gain of 10.59 dBic at 1.58 GHz and a front-to-back ratio > 25 dB. This antenna can be applicable in Global Positioning Systems (GPS) and satellite communication systems.

articleTitle: Metasurface-based Triangle Patch Antenna with Moon Shape Slot for Multi-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a multi-band circularly polarized triangle patch antenna loaded with a metasurface. The design comprises two layers stacked on each other where the upper layer contains a 4x4 square corner truncated metasurface and the lower substrate contains an equilateral triangle patch with triangular and moon-shaped slots. The proposed antenna over all dimensions are 43x42x3.15 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The operating frequencies and the bandwidth offered by the proposed antenna are 360 MHz (5.47-5.83 GHz), 680 MHz (8.01-8.69 GHz), 490 MHz (10.03-10.52 GHz), 680 MHz (11.95-12.63 GHz), and 4.61 GHz (13.39-18 GHz) with a peak gain of 7.07dBi at 15.76 GHz.The antenna offers an axial ratio bandwidth of 100 MHz (15.08-15.18 GHz). The antenna suitable for multiband applications. Simulations were carried out using Ansys HFSS software.

articleTitle: Broadband Low Noise Amplifier Design For Optimal Noise and Impedance Matching
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a 1-10GHz broadband multistage monolithic microwave integrated circuit low noise amplifier using 250nm GaAs pseudo-morphic high electron mobility transistor process of UMS foundry. Shunt negative feedback and inductive source degeneration techniques are used simultaneously to achieve wideband gain response, low noise along with good impedance matching over the entire band. Simulation results show 2.3dB noise figure, average gain of 17dB, return loss better than 12dB, and output 1 dB compression of 14-10 dBm over the entire 1-10GHz frequency band. The LNA is realized within the footprint of 1.7x2.7x0.1 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and consumes only 198mW of power.

articleTitle: Study on Resonant Microstrip Line Coupled to a Double-gap Split Ring Resonator for Various Microwave Filter Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A resonant microstrip line (MTL) based on a square-shaped double-gap split ring resonator (DSRR), with parallel split-gaps placed symmetrically on opposite sides, is studied for various types of microwave filter applications. At first, a mode-splitting characteristic is observed for a DSRR loaded resonant microstrip line. Then, variation of rejection depth with resonance frequency are examined with variation of side-length and split-gap as well as with coupling distances between MTL and SRR, keeping other parameters constant. Depending on parameters of this coupled system, characteristics pertaining to a notch filter, a band-stop filter and also, a dual-band stop filter are obtained for microwave device applications.

articleTitle: Wideband Antenna Array for 5G mmWave Mobile Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this article, we introduce a wide-band quasi-Yagi antenna and its proposed 4x1 array system with radio wave propagation analysis for mm-Wave 5G mobile terminals. The suggested antenna array is designed using a basic planar Quasi-Yagi-Uda topology so that it may be incorporated into 5G mobile terminals. A single antenna with a gain of 7.65 dBi at 24 GHz and 8.37 dBi at 28 GHz with a reflection coefficient (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf><-10dB) of 26% (23-30 GHz). A pair of 4x1 linear quasi-Yagi antenna arrays have also been integrated into the mobile terminal's top and right-side frames. The proposed array configurations can occupy an overall size of 66×46×0.254 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> with 0.7λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> center-to-center element spacing and have a low mutual coupling of -40 dB obtained for antenna arrays. The results demonstrate that the proposed two separate 4x1 linear quasi-Yagi antenna arrays exhibit peak gains of 14 dBi and 15 dBi at frequencies of 24 GHz and 28 GHz, respectively, and a broad impedance bandwidth covering the 5G-n258 frequency band. Radio wave propagation analysis and virtual drive test are performed with antenna radiation performance. With the above radiation characteristics, the proposed antenna is an ideal solution for 5G millimeter-Wave cellular terminals applications.

articleTitle: Wide Angular Stable Textile Microwave Absorber for False Image Reduction in Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A textile based microwave absorber (TMA) operating in the 24 GHz band is presented in this paper. Wide anglular stability is achieved by connecting two back-to-back square meander rings using a narrow metallic strip. The operational bandwidth is significantly widened by using these integrated meandered structures to cover the 24 GHz autonomous vehicular communication band. Peak absorption ratio of > 98% is achieved over the entire operating range from 21.5 - 35.6 GHz and the performance is verified for different textile based fabrics such as felt, cotton and jeans. Compared to the conventional/flat substrate materials, the proposed TMA is polarization insensitive, has wide angular stability (up to 60°) and conformal features. With these advantages, the absorber in this study is suitable for installation on vehicle roof-top for false image reduction. The measured results are in excellent agreement with the simulations.

articleTitle: Phased Array Antenna Design and Analysis Tool
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this work we have implemented the phased array design equations and guidelines to obtain an interface for quick and reasonable computation of the array design parameters based on the requirements. These equations could be used to obtain an initial design without the need for simulations. Impact of various design parameters on the array performance has been analyzed and results are presented.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Wideband 2-Way Power Divider for Space Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A compact and wideband two-way equal Wilkinson power divider with operating frequency range of 3 to 6 GHz for space applications using microstrip structure is presented in this paper. Compared with conventional microstrip power dividers, this power divider utilizes only single section and optimum impedance transforming network to achieve wide bandwidth. The limiting effect of isolation resistor pads is analyzed and the parasitic pad capacitances are compensated by the proposed structure. The power divider is realized on 25mil alumina substrate in small size of 12.5mm X 12.5mm. Broadband characteristic of the proposed power divider is verified by experimental results. Measurements of the fabricated divider showed input and output return losses better than 13dB with low insertion loss of 0.35-0.55dB and typical isolation better than 14dB over the design bandwidth.

articleTitle: A Super-Wideband Multiband MIMO Antenna for Microwave and Millimeter Wave Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This communication reports a multi-super-wideband microwave-access antenna that achieves a bandwidth of 8.56GHz-39.02GHz and finds applications for X-band, Ku-band in Microwave and 28.0GHz & 38.0GHz for millimeter-Wave band 5G infrastructure. The patch which radiates electromagnetic energy consists of a hexagon shape with partial rectangular ground printed on Rogers-Substrate with a thin thickness of 0.254mm. The proposed work with a single element occupies a very compact space of 120 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> and the MIMO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SWB</inf> counterpart occupies a space of 240 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The proposed antenna releasing EM wave offers an average peak realized gain of 4.74dBi and directivity of 4.09dB. The proposed antenna also offers desirable 2-D radiation patterns at 10.60GHz, 16.0GHz, 28.0GHz, and 38.0GHz respectively. The MIMO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SWB</inf> configuration with an edge-to-edge spacing of 2.50mm achieves isolation of more than 12.50dB with diversity parameters ECC<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SWB</inf><0.12, DG<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SWB</inf>>9.995dB, TARC<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SWB</inf><-27.50dB and CCL<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">SWB</inf><0.30b/s/Hz. The antenna radiating technology achieving several useable bands is useful in mobile networks for achieving information and communication system.

articleTitle: A Spectrally Efficient MIMO System with Sparse Matrix Precoding
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel technique of sparse matrix based precoding at the transmitter of a Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) system. Our proposal, which we have called SMP-MIMO (Sparse Matrix Precoded MIMO), uses a two-layer precoding approach in which the conventional zero-forcing (ZF) MIMO precoder, which inverts the matrix MIMO channel, is combined with a sparse matrix precoding. With the conventional ZF precoder, the degrees of freedom (DoF) available at the transmitter equals the number of antennas at the receiver. By adding another layer of precoding using a sparse matrix, we increase the DoF at the transmitter, thereby facilitating an increase in the spectral efficiency compared to the ZF-precoded MIMO. We demonstrate a proof of the SMP-MIMO concept (PoC) by simulation-driven experiments. Our PoC is based on the ML (Maximum Likelihood) detection at the receiver. The resulting computational complexity can be reduced by applying a compressive sensing algorithm or a belief propagation algorithm that leverages the sparseness of the precoding matrix.

articleTitle: S/Ka- Band Shared Aperture Antenna System for Data Relay Satellites and Ground Station Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Antenna systems operating in widely separated dual/triple bands are becoming common requirements owing to various complex mission requirements. In this work, a Dual CP, Dual Band shared aperture feed system is developed that feeds a reflector system in Axially Displaced Configuration. S-Band CP horn operates in coaxial TE11 mode where as Ka-Band CP Horn operates in conventional circular waveguide TE11 mode. Concentric phase centres, appropriate illumination taper, dual CP operation, tracking mode using higher order TM01 are some of the salient features of this work. The designed Antenna System exhibits a gain of > 31.1 dBi and 31.8 dBi in S-Band Tx, Rx with Axial Ratio < 2 dB. At Ka-Band, the Antenna system exhibits a gain of >52.1 dBi and 53.4 dBi in Tx, Rx Bands with Axial Ratio < 2 dB. Tracking pattern null depth of > 40 dB is seen in secondary pattern.

articleTitle: Tunable Magnetic Material based Composite Microwave Absorber for Stealth Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Microwave-absorbing materials have attracted significant interest over many years for their applications in civilian as well as defense fields. On this account, rigorous research is going on for the development of efficient microwave absorbers. However, it is not easy to develop a tunable microwave absorber as per user demand. Therefore, this paper presents magnetic material-based composites which can be tuned at a particular frequency in the S and C-band on the mixing of particular wt.% of carbonyl iron in milled cobalt powder. Their preparation method is very simple using a high-energy ball mill. The results showed the absorption of all synthesized samples in the S, C, and X-band. The maximum tunability is found to be 63.76% when only 20 wt.% of carbonyl iron was mixed in milled cobalt powder.

articleTitle: Antenna Systems for On-Orbit Reconfiguration of Beams
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: On-orbit reconfiguration of coverage beams is often required for military satellites as well as commercial satellites due to changes in operational scenarios. This paper describes various reconfigurable antenna systems providing the required flexibility on-orbit. Phased array and imaging reflector systems are suitable for mobile and military systems while mechanical articulation is more preferred for contoured beam antennas for fixed satellite and broadcast satellite services. Details of antenna designs and RF performance are given in this paper.

articleTitle: Design of Printed Monopole Array Antenna with Decoupling Network For MIMO Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This manuscript presents the design of a decoupling network and its integration with the tightly coupled printed monopole array antenna at the L-band. The manuscript describes the design flow, its related aspects for such a network and its use with array elements. The proposed monopole array antenna with decoupling network has shown ~17.54dB improvement in the mutual coupling between elements at resonating frequency and shown consistent element-wise radiation pattern properties compared to the array antenna without decoupling network. Moreover, the array antenna with decoupling network has also been evaluated for multiple inputs multiple outputs (MIMO) application, where the envelop correlation factor has been computed and compared. The presented array antenna with decoupling network offers ~0.00 envelop correlation factor at 1.26GHz frequency, which is significantly low.

articleTitle: Beam-steering Transmitarray Antenna for 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this work, a linearly polarized, high gain, low profile, symmetrical metasurface-based transmitarray antenna is presented. To design the transmitarray, two RT/duroid 5880 substrates of thickness 0.787 mm are sandwiched between three conducting layers. The geometry of conducting layers in the unit cell is altered accordingly to obtain the desired phase shifting characteristics. These unit cells are then arranged in a particular fashion, obtained from the phase difference equation, to make the transmitarray. The transmitarray is illuminated by a 2×2 microstrip patch antenna array placed at the focal distance (D = 43.2 mm). The F/D ratio of the design is 0.8 which makes it a low-profile antenna. Beam-steering is achieved by moving the feed source along the focal plane. The design transmitarray antenna operates in 25.2-30.5 GHz (BW=19%) band having bandwidth 5.3 GHz. The simulation results show a maximum gain of 17.7 dBi in the broadside direction, scan angle is 46° (-23° to +23°) in both the E-plane and H-plane, with a scan loss of 1.45 dB.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Circular patch antenna for Wi-Fi 7 and 5G applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper present the design & simulation of slotted – circular Micro strip patch antennas which is resonate at 6.5 GHz and 3.5GHz frequencies. The first slotted circular patch antenna operated at 6.5 GHz frequency, which is lies in between (5.925GHz-7.1GHz) of 6GHz frequency band. This frequency range is suitable for future wireless application i.e. Wi-Fi 7. Also other two designs of single slotted – circular Micro strip patch antenna element & its 2×1 element array were implemented and both designs operated at 3.5 GHz frequency & falls in between (3.3GHz- 4.2GHz) band and this range is the birth place of 5<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">th</sup> generation communication (5G).The presented antennas were design and simulated by HFSS software.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Microstrip Dipole Antenna Stacked on a PV Panel for Dual-Energy Harvesting
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The proposed work demonstrates a simulation-based study on implementation of dual-energy harvesting system using solar cells and antenna. To study and analyze the feasibility initially the design of a simple planar dipole antenna on a FR4 substrate of 80 x 40 x 1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> was done. Later the single element antenna was intended use in conjunction with a solar cell. The resultant structure will be the solar cell will be on the top side in order to capture the solar energy and the antenna will be backside of the solar cell. The sandwich structural elements during integration of solar cell with antenna are also considered during simulation in order to analyze the effects on return loss and resonant frequencies of the antenna due to the stacked layers involved (Epoxy/Kevlar, Silicon and FR4 Substrates). The array implementations were done in 1x2, 1x4 and 2x2 configuration in order to increase the gain of the antenna so as to capture the EM energy in the respective bands across 4.1 GHz, 6.1 GHz and 7.6 GHz respectively. The simulation results proves that the antenna has good gain of 5.74 dB at 7.6 GHz (in 1x2 array configuration), 5.63 dB at 7.63 GHz (in 2x2 array configuration) and 4.67 dB at 7.42 GHz band (in 1x4 array configuration) makes the antenna suitable for operating in C-band and thus able to harvest the EM energy along with the solar energy harvesting system in the same structure.

articleTitle: Time Variant Circularly Polarized CPW Antenna for WIFI/ISM/Wi-Max/Wi-LAN Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A Triple band triple sensed CPW-Fed Circularly polarized Antenna is presented in this article. The rectangular parasitic elements mainly responsible for the generation of circular polarization (LCHP, RCHP) in lower (2.4GHz) and upper (5.8GHz) bands. The antenna covers modern commercial applications such as 2.4GHz (Wi-Fi band), 3.5GHz (WI-MAX),5.8GHz(WLAN) Applications. The proposed model gives Triple band circular polarization of below 3dB axial ratio tells proposed model is a good candidate for Targeted applications.

articleTitle: A Triple Band Polarization Insensitive Metamaterial Absorber for Terahertz Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A miniaturized unit cell structure design for THz metamaterial absorber for triple band absorption is presented in this paper. Lossy polyimide substrate is used for developing the unit cell structure which consists of two resonators. The miniaturized footprint of the unit cell structure is given by 0.104λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>×0.104λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> represents the effective wavelength which is being calculated at lowest frequency of absorption. The first resonator of the unit cell structure includes the outer square ring whereas the second resonator consists of S-shaped structures placed at one diagonal position and the other diagonal position is comprised of the same S-shaped structure placed after rotating it leftwards. The unit cell structure provides three absorption bands of 95.868%, 94.691% and 95.434% at 0.347, 0.834 and 0.935 THz respectively. For these frequency ranges the suggested metamaterial absorber possesses various applications in the field of THz imaging, filtering, biological sensing, and optical communications. As the proposed structure has a four-fold symmetry, it reflects similar results for various angles of polarization in TE mode.

articleTitle: A Wideband Design of Circularly Polarized Antenna With High Gain
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A high gain design of the circularly polarized (CP) antenna is proposed to achieve wide axial-ratio (AR) bandwidth. A sequential rotation technique is employed to excite the array of four microstrip patches with dual-offset feeding. Significant improvement in CP gain is achieved by using a strategically designed metallic wall. The AR remains below 1dB over the 52.5% (8.54−14.62 GHz) impedance bandwidth of the antenna, indicating a 52.5% AR bandwidth. Over the entire operating frequency band, the left-handed CP (LHCP) gain remains above 11.2 dBic and reaches 14.84 dBic at 13GHz. The LHCP gain can be enhanced by approximately 4 dB by using the metallic wall. Cross-polar discrimination (XPD) is better than 35dB and can reach up to 54dB. The AR beamwidth is approximately 28° or more and shows the CP coverage around the boresight direction.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of mm-wave Dual Band Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a study of mm-Wave textile-based antenna for health care applications is presented. The antenna operating in the mm-wave range at 45 and 65GHz is analyzed. A cotton-based textile substrate with a thickness of 1.5mm and with the dimensions 7.0 × 4.5 ×1.5 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> is proposed. The radiating patch has a tuning fork-shaped semi-circle of radius 1mm. The cotton substrate is used because it has low relative permittivity and low surface loss with improved impedance bandwidth. The ground plane attached to the bottom of the substrate has slots covering the radiating patch antenna on the opposite side to improve the matching and the impedance bandwidth. The presence of the ground plane minimizes the back radiation to the human body. The mm-Wave antenna operates from (45-65)GHz with a return loss of 14dB at 45GHz and 30dB at 65GHz is observed. The resonating frequency is independent of the length of the antenna and the radiating patch. The tiny cotton-based textile antenna is useful for body-centric communications. The antenna is also used for e-health applications.

articleTitle: A Compact Polarization Insensitive Triple-band Artificial Magnetic Conductor using Complementary Structures
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents the design of a compact triple-band artificial magnetic conductor using stacking of the complementary structure. The proposed triple-band complementary AMC is formed by combining the cross-shaped structure with three stubs of different lengths at each arm on one dielectric slab and its complementary geometry on the other dielectric slab. The proposed AMC provides the three 0° degree reflection phase frequencies at 2.45 GHz, 3.5 GHz, and 5.99 GHz with a ±90° reflection phase bandwidth of 0.2 GHz, 0.17 GHz, and 0.94 GHz, respectively. The unit cell size is 13 mm×13 mm (0.1λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>×0.1λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>), where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the wavelength at the lowest resonance frequency of 2.45 GHz. The proposed structure is insensitive to incident polarization and angles due to the four-fold symmetry of the unit cell. In addition, on rotating the complementary structure, the AMC unit cell exhibits the two closely spaced reflection phase frequencies.

articleTitle: RealD3: A Real-time Driver Drowsiness Detection Scheme Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Drowsiness has become a major problem in people’s lives, resulting in ineffective work or traffic accidents. Every year the rate of injuries and accidents increases due to the drowsiness of drivers around the world. Therefore, developing a real-time driver drowsiness detection system is a current necessity. This paper presents a real-time driver drowsiness detection scheme (RealD3) that uses advanced machine learning algorithms for prediction. The main aim of this work is to detect and analyze the facial structure and objects in the frame. To capture the driver’s face, a camera-based video-capturing mechanism is used. Mediapipe face mesh 468 and YOLO (You Only Look Once) are used for detecting landmarks and facial features in the frame, respectively. Once face, landmark, and facial features (such as Eye Aspect Ratio (EAR), Mouth Aspect Ratio (MAR), Hands on Mouth, and if sunglasses are worn or not ) get detected, PERCLOS is used for classifying if the driver is drowsy or simply blinking. An alert is given to the driver when the EAR and MAR values are less than the threshold value and YOLO detects drowsiness based on the facial features. The real-time experimental results show that the proposed method is highly accurate and advanced, with an overall accuracy of about 94% in detecting drowsiness and identifying objects in the frame.

articleTitle: Split Ring Resonator Based Isolation Reduced 5g MIMO Antenna for UWB Communication Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A Metamaterial inspired 5G MIMO antenna is proposed in this article. Proposed work done on FR4 substrate having thickness of 1.6 mm using ANSYS EM Tools. proposed model works between 2-12 GH covering all commercial and x- band applications. The designed antenna is tested for its reliability to use at modern 5G applications. The simulated results and its properties show proposed work can be highly used for 5G applications.

articleTitle: A Multiband Rhombus Shaped Patch Antenna with Rhombus Slots for C, X, and Ku-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A multiband rhombus-shaped patch antenna with rhombus slots is presented in this paper. The dimensions of the proposed antenna are 50x48x1.2mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> at the operating frequency is 5.54GHz. The rhombus patch antenna with rhombus slots results in a multiband operation operating in a bandwidth of 80MHz (6.60GHz to 6.68GHz), 80MHz (8.36GHz to 8.44GHz), 400MHz (12.65GHz to 13.05GHz), 450MHz (14.76GHz to 15.21GHz), and 990MHz (16.73GHz to 17.72GHz) with a peak gain of 6.02dBi at 12.88GHz and exhibits circular polarization at the frequency range of 15.56GHz to 15.77GHz. The proposed antenna is suitable for C, X, and Ku-band applications. Simulations are carried out using Ansys HFSS software.

articleTitle: Dual Frequency Center Fed Dipole Antenna with Trap Circuit For Radio Beacon Ionospheric Study
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of dual frequency deployable antenna system which works at 150MHz & 400MHz frequencies for study of Total Electron Content (TEC) of Ionosphere [1]. The TEC is derived from the phase difference between two electromagnetic waves as it propagates from onboard beacon through the ionosphere to ground receivers. Concept of center-fed half-wave dipole configuration with trap circuit is adopted for the Antenna design. It consists of a dipole antenna with two passive reflectors, mounted on satellite of size 600x600mm. A single antenna with trap circuit introduced at appropriate distance from the feed point on either side will enable the dual frequency operation. Trap is a parallel tuned circuit, which offers very high impedance at UHF (400MHz) and almost a zero impedance at VHF (150MHz). Antenna is designed to transmit 400MHz and 150MHz frequencies simultaneously. Balun is also designed for enabling dual frequency operation. Realization aspects and measured results of this antenna are discussed here. The measured gain at 400MHz frequency is 8.5dBi and at 150MHz frequency is 7.0 dBi. This antenna system was mounted on micro-satellite.During launch phase, antenna elements were kept at stowed condition by means of Nylon rope tying over tubes and release of antenna elements is achieved by fusing the rope, using Nichrome wire. The torsion springs provided at the hinges supply necessary energy for deployment of the antenna tubes.

articleTitle: Frequency Adaptable Antenna for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This antenna’s structure is made up of a stub-loaded circular radiator and slot etching procedures on a FR-4 epoxy (ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> = 2.2) with a thickness of 0.254 mm and a resonant frequency of 5.4GHz. The proposed design consists of a compact frequency reconfigurable antenna for flexible devices and conformal surfaces. The gain of the proposed antenna (2.5 dBi) is significantly higher than the existing prototype antenna. The functioning of the designed antenna in the desired frequency range is successfully analyzed. The antenna can find applications in Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Satellite Communications.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Slotted Ultra-Wide Band Antenna for WiMAX and WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: An Ultra Wide Band (UWB) antenna is presented using the slots over the surface of microstrip patch antenna. The antenna resonates from 3.21 GHz to 11.56 GHz frequencies having the bandwidth of 113 % with moderate gain of 4.81 dBi. The additional notches are provided at the four corners of patch geometry. An extra thin vertical slot is also developed between the two vertical boundaries of feeding structure. The FR4 is utilized as substrate material which is cost effective. The discussed structure is appropriate for WiMAX and WLAN applications.

articleTitle: A Graphene Patch Antenna with Improved Performance for THz Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of a miniaturized, efficient graphene-based antenna working in the terahertz (THz) domain. The top radiating patch of square-shaped graphene is designed over silicon dioxide (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) substrate while the bottom surface is grounded with gold. The proposed antenna operates over the lower THz frequency bands of 1.3 THz to 2.73 THz and 2.75 THz to 3.01 THz with the maximum return loss of 27 dB at 2.24 THz. The antenna achieves the realized gain of 6.94 dBi at 2.56 THz and provides directional radiation characteristics in both the E- and H-planes. The proposed antenna further exhibits the beam scanning feature over a range close to 32°. The proposed graphene-based antenna is compact, directive, and highly efficient in the THz domain. It finds useful applications in biomedical, satellite communication, high-quality video imaging etc.

articleTitle: Dual-Facet Loaded Dual-Polarized Quad-band Dielectric Resonator-Rectenna for RF Energy Harvesting in Smart City Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The most widely used approach for replacing traditional batteries and extending battery life is radio frequency energy harvesting (RFEH). However, the power density in the immediate environment is low thus the antenna with multiband features is essential to gather a huge amount of RF power from the low-density atmosphere. This paper presented a multiband dual-polarized dielectric resonator antenna for smart city applications using RFEH technology. The proposed DR antenna covers the frequency bands of WLAN 5.2 GHz, Wi-Fi 5.8 GHz, and future 6 GHz Wi-Fi bands of 6.2 GHz and 6.6 GHz. A rectangular dielectric resonator (DR) is fabricated using a K10 material and it is designed on a low-cost epoxy FR4 substrate (having ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf>=4.4). A coaxial probe feeding approach is used for excitation purposes. The substrate and DR material dimensions are 66 mm×68.2 mm×1.6 mm and 13.6 mm×11.4 mm×6.35 mm respectively. A spiral metallic coil is stuck on two faces (front and bottom) of a DR material to operate the antenna in the desired band of frequencies. The proposed technique is used to bring down the axial ratio (AR) value below 3dB level in two resonant bands. The maximum gain of 6.72 dB is observed experimentally at 5.2 GHz frequency.

articleTitle: Microstrip Patch Antenna For Full Duplex Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In-band full duplex (IBFD) communication is a potential technology currently investigated for 5G networks to increase the spectrum efficiency. It demands maximum self-interference cancellation at antenna stage of the system for providing good isolation. This paper communicates a dual linear polarized three port square microstrip antenna. It is differentially excited with 180° hybrid ring coupler for providing high inter-port isolation. The proposed antenna along with 180° hybrid ring coupler operating at 2.4GHz is printed on 1.6 mm thick FR4 Epoxy substrate. The simulated and measured results show that impedance bandwidth, interport isolation, return loss at two ports are 60MHz, -61dB, -15dB -13dB and 60 MHz,-56 dB, -14dB, -15dB respectively. Radiation characteristics with good co polarization and cross polarization characteristics are attained. A good concurrence is viewed between the simulation and experimental results confirming the use of antenna to be a promising contestant for full duplex communication applications with single carrier frequency for transmitting and receiving.

articleTitle: Design of a THz Antenna with Broadband Radiation Characteristics for 6G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, the design of a Terahertz (THz) antenna for broadband wireless high-data-rate communication is proposed. Several antenna designs are presented here that are better suited to short-range THz communication in 6G applications. The initial implementation will be a 310 GHz single-element dipole reflector antenna. With a gain of 4.82 dBi, this antenna can cover the frequency range of 295 GHz to 400 GHz with an impedance bandwidth of 33.8%. Second, to improve gain while keeping nearly the same impedance bandwidth, a new design is presented that is based on the same dipole structure but adds directors in the shape of a half circle. When three half-circle-shaped directors are used, the gain increases to 7.27 dBi. All in all, the results obtained make the proposed designs strong contenders for 6G wireless communication systems that prioritize speed over range.

articleTitle: A broadband transition design between coplanar waveguide and air-filled substrate integrated waveguides for millimeter-wave applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This work proposes a broadband transition between grounded coplanar waveguide to air-filled substrate integrated waveguide based on super-ellipse geometry for millimeter wave applications. Based on the order of the super-ellipse, two configurations are possible: a triangular and a semi-elliptical geometry. Back-to-back transitions in both configurations are designed to operate in K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>-band. Both transitions offer a return loss better than 13 dB and an insertion loss less than 0.7 dB in the operating band. Further, the performance of the air-filled SIW is analyzed to quantify the attenuation constant, phase constant, and group delay. The loss due to each transition is computed using the post-processing data. The performance of the air-filled SIW is suitable to be used in millimeter-wave applications, and the proposed transitions also work well with the structure offering minimum insertion loss and good matching.

articleTitle: Experimental Characterization of Simulated PIFA Designed by Parametric Design Methodology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A verification of characterization of simulated PIFA designed by parametric design approach. The optimized dimensions derived from parametric simulation studies are considered for fabrication of real PIFA. Characterization parameters of the fabricated PIFA such as return loss (S11), VSWR, bandwidth (Δf), and impedance (Z) over the desired frequency band were measured. Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) was used to carry out the measured over the frequency range of 3 to 4 GHz. The antenna radiation characteristics were also obtained using anechoic chamber for E-filed and H-field measurements in same frequency range. The experimental and simulated PIFA characteristic parameters exited good agreement.

articleTitle: A Single Layered High Gain and Broadband Antenna with H-Shaped Patch and Meta Patches for 5GHz Wi-Fi Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The broadband linearly polarized antenna with high gain in single layered substrate is designed using H shaped patch with meta patches and uniform aperture CPW feed. Initially, the slot antenna is designed with bi-directional radiation. The H shaped patch is placed on another side of slot to design unidirectional pattern with an impedance bandwidth of 7% (5.21-5.59GHz) and the gain of antenna is 7.5-7.7 dBi. The meta patches are added around the H shaped patch to increase the gain and impedance bandwidth simultaneously. The above-mentioned antenna achieved an impedance bandwidth of 34.1% (4.50-6.35GHz) and gain of antenna 10-11.3dB.

articleTitle: Design of Compact Fed Serrated CPW Radial Patch Antenna for WiMAX Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this article, A coplanar waveguide (CPW) fed monopole antenna is presented. The antenna is built using FR4 substrate of size 30x30x1.6. The proposed antenna works at single band having compact size of 30*30. Artificial Magnetic Conductors (AMC)structures are used to provide a better bandwidth enhancement to make use of the antenna to work in WIMAX (3.5GHz) Applications. To enable fast data transfer and competitivity among many users for communication systems WiMAX bands acts as a bridge. The proposed work is carried out iteration wise to get works at targeted band. The practicality of the proposed work is verified using the simulated results in ANSYS HFSS. The radiation patterns, reflection coefficients and other antenna parameters their analysis have been verified according to the WiMAX standards.

articleTitle: Polarization Converter Metamaterial Structure for X/Ku/K Bands
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A single layer polarization converter (PCR) based metasurface unit cell is proposed using FR-4 substrate of thickness 2.4 mm and periodicity of 7.75 mm. The proposed design obtained frequency band of 9.7 – 19.05 GHz with PCR value above 90%. The unit cell has been investigated for both TE and TM polarization modes and for oblique incidences.

articleTitle: High Gain Low Axial-Ratio Circularly Polarized Dual-PRS Fabry-Perot Cavity Antenna at S-Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A high-gain all-metallic dual-PRS Cross-dipole fed Circularly Polarized Fabry-Perot Cavity Antenna (CP-FPCA) with low axial-ratio and symmetric radiation pattern is presented in this paper. Cavity-backed ground plane and cross-dipole elements are optimally configured with dual-layer PRS of the FPC to simultaneously achieve high performance including gain of 17.0-18.5dBi, axial-ratio < 1.5dB and Return-loss < -15dB over 2.56-2.68GHz S-band transmit-receive frequency band.

articleTitle: Real Time Measurement of Hotspots Electric field components using EMF Detector
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In certain scenario, a situation crisis where the signal strength is poor. This problem majority focus on finding the root cause of signal fading due to effects of interference or the external noise environment. Initially, the approach is to locate the hotspots across the college campus. Then fixing the origin at one hotspot, different hotspots will be configured in different places with 3-axis coordinate points (x, y, z) through the field work.
