Further, an EMF detector is used to read the instant real time axis points at positional hotspots which display the values of RF, EMF & EF. These tabulated values at different hotspots will evaluate to understand the field strength levels categorized as low, modern & high.

articleTitle: 11-13.6 GHz Wideband Compact High Gain MMIC Amplifier for Radar Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper describes the design, development and measurement results of wideband and high gain compact monolithic microwave integrated circuit amplifier for Ku-band applications. The MMIC fabricated on 0.25µm GaAs p-HEMT technology, is a two-stage common source design where negative feedback is used to achieve wideband performance. The proposed amplifier demonstrates minimum gain of 24 dB with gain flatness of less than ±0.5dB over the entire frequency band of operation. The MMIC amplifier consumes only 252mW of power and has an option of bias distribution on two opposite sides of circuit for integration ease. The compact amplifier fits into 3mm x 2.6mm x 0.1mm of small formfactor.

articleTitle: Design of FSS based Low Observable Antenna-Radome System for Aerospace Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, EM design and analysis of FSS-based low observable antenna-radome system is presented for aerospace application, where FSS-based novel rasorber is used as superstrate of antenna. The rasorber consists of a lossy resistive layer and a band pass FSS-layer separated by a foam spacer. The resistive layer has slotted circular ring FSS printed on top of the dielectric and gridded Jerusalem cross FSS structure on the other side of it. The band pass FSS layer having gridded simple cross dipole is used at the bottom to provide ground plane properties. The proposed antenna-rasorber system is analyzed using commercial EM design software HFSS V.2021R2. The proposed FSS-rasorber exhibits broadband transmission from 8.65 GHz to 10.8 GHz with respect to 1 dB insertion loss, due to impedance matching at parallel resonance. It shows good absorption more than 80% from 13.6 GHz to 18 GHz with maximum absorption of 97.6% at 14.3 GHz, where resistive layer plays an important role. Further, the FSS-rasorber structure is used as superstrate of microstrip patch antenna array showing significant reduction of its radar cross section (RCS) without affecting the gain of antenna array in transmission band.

articleTitle: VHF Active Phased Pilot Array Radar for Atmospheric Remote Sensing Applications at University of Calcutta
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A fully functional Pilot active phased array radar operating at 53 MHz is installed at University of Calcutta, Kolkata, India. The pilot array comprising of 19 number three element Yagi-Uda antennas used to sense the atmospheric winds up to an altitude range of 8-10 km. The horizontal winds measured from the pilot array are compared with the collocated GPS radiosonde balloon measurements and a good correspondence has been observed between the two measurements.

articleTitle: Contoured Beam Analysis of Satellite Antenna Directivity and GAP
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Contoured beams are widely used for fixed satellite and broadcast satellite services from geostationary earth orbits (GEO). They provide uplink receive and downlink transmit beams from a single antenna where they are shaped to fit close to the geographic coverage region. This paper presents Gaussian beam analysis to predict the minimum coverage area directivity without running time-consuming RF analysis. This analysis is shown to predict antenna directivity values close to more accurate analysis through TICRA software. The analysis is applicable for both contoured beam and spot beam antenna directivity predictions.

articleTitle: Pixellated Metasurface for Effective Absorption of Electromagnetic Wave at Desired Frequency
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A optimization technique is used to design two pixel-lated metasurface absorbers to work in frequency ranges: 2-5 GHz and 6-8 GHz using CST Microwave Studio. The absorber is made up of copper patched pixels on FR4 substrate and a copper backing layer. Particle swarm optimization is used to decide the structural parameters of the absorber. Numerical results show a peak absorptance frequency of 2.85 GHz for metasurface 1 and 6.8 GHz for metasurface 2, with peak absorptance values of 0.98 and 0.99, respectively. The range of frequency over which the absorptance remains more than 0.9 is 200-MHz and 100-MHz for metasurface 1 and 2, respectively.

articleTitle: Central E shaped stub loaded stepped impedance resonator for multiband filter application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a multiband filter using two centrally E shaped stub loaded stepped impedance resonator (SLSIR) is presented. Due to the presence of stub loading in the single mode open loop ring resonator, dual mode is achieved. The band pass responses are achieved due to the fundamental odd and fundamental even mode resonant frequency and also with first three even mode higher order resonant frequencies. The four center frequencies are located at 0.90 GHz, 2.08 GHz, 3.40 GHz and 4.60 GHz and fractional bandwidths are 16.7%. 6.96%, 5.84%, 1.79% respectively. Also return loss exceeds 15.35 dB and insertion loss is underneath 0.92 dB.

articleTitle: Machine Learning based Non-Cooperative Target Recognition with Dynamic RCS Data
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: There is ever increasing requirement of identification of non-cooperative aerial targets for ensuring flight safety, security, and effective airspace management. The identification or classification can be done by utilizing target features and estimated Radar Cross Section (RCS) obtained from modern multifunction phased array radars. The estimated RCS is dependent on various governing factors, and it is significantly stochastic in nature. In this paper authors propose to implement machine learning algorithms on the dynamic RCS for radar target identification. We have considered three fixed wing aerial targets of sizes 3.7 m, 7.5 m and 14.9 m for classification. Time varying RCS or dynamic RCS for these targets has been generated based on aspect angle derived from flight path as reported by Automatic Dependent Surveillance-Broadcast (ADS-B) data source and interlinking the same with EM solver generated RCS value. The classification accuracy of 97.4 %, 63.5% and 66.3 % has been obtained while using Random Forest, Support Vector Machine and Adaptive Boosting Algorithm respectively.

articleTitle: Design of Dielectric Resonator Based Low Profile Dual Band Antenna for Wlan and C Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A low-profile dual-band cylindrical dielectric resonator antenna(CDRA) with a defected ground surface (DGS) is discussed in this article. Wide bandwidth is achieved by creating three modified dumbbell-shaped slots in the ground plane. The CDRA is placed over a square ring patch feed with a microstrip line feeding to resonate at two resonant frequencies 5.32 GHz and 7.63 GHz. The presented antenna has a bandwidth of 210 MHz at lower resonance and bandwidth of 290 MHz at higher resonance exhibits |S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>| < −15 dB and has peak gains of 8 dBi at 5.32 GHz and 5 dBi at 7.63 GHz respectively. This radiating system is a good candidate for the WLAN (5.32 GHz), S-band applications like airport surveillance, and C-Band applications.

articleTitle: Broadband blade antenna operating in UHF band for ELT application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a UHF band blade antenna is presented especially for ELT beacons, used mainly for search and rescue operations supported by the COSAPS SARSAT satellite constellations. The detailed design procedure to achieve broadband behaviour and the parametric analysis of all the geometric parameters are discussed. Proposed antenna is developed on a FR4 substrate and its RF characterization is carried out. It has a 10dB return loss bandwidth of 60% at 406MHz. Proposed antenna is a linearly polarized antenna with gain better than 1.5dBi and cross polarization isolation better than 30dB throughout the band.

articleTitle: Data Analysis of U-blox GPS on Static and Dynamic Drone Platform
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Purpose of U Blox is to provide GPS coordinates for satellite-based navigation system. In essence, U-Blox creates and manufactures chips and modules that enables global navigation satellite systems (GNSS), including receivers for GPS, GLONASS, Galileo, BeiDou, and QZSS. Most of the U-Blox based applications are real-time surveillance, where accurate position is required for navigation. U-Blox supports universal access that provides easy connect with any satellite system with the help of NMEA data. The aim of this paper is to review of U-Blox GPS on Static and Dynamic Drone platform to give a basic and in-depth insights to reader.

articleTitle: A Polarization Insensitive Dual-functional Vanadium Dioxide (VO2)-based Metasurface Structure in the Terahertz Gap
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A polarization insensitive dual-functional vanadium dioxide (VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>)-based metasurface structure has been proposed in this communication. It can provide both transmission and absorption of electromagnetic wave at the same frequency band under different thermal excitations. Periodically arranged VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> square rings have been designed on a silicon dioxide (SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) substrate backed by a gold layer comprising periodic square ring slots filled with VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>. The proposed structure offers transparency with 92.69% transmission coefficient at 1 THz under room temperature. The same device works as an absorber with absorptivity around 99.75% at the identical frequency when the temperature reaches to 68°C. It offers angular stability up to 40° for both transmission and absorption performances.

articleTitle: Review on Wireless Charging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a review of the currently existing technology of wireless charging, with a brief insight into up-and-coming improvements and variations related to it. While wireless technology is currently being used in multiple fields or has research being conducted on, this paper, focuses on the types, the scope of use, and domains it's currently being used in. Wireless charging, in essence, is getting rid of the cable or physical connection between the charger and the device getting charged. The flow of energy is established without any physical connection. It has various methods depending on the domain of use.

articleTitle: A Learning Based Approach for Intelligent Reflecting Surface (IRS) Assisted Return Link Beamforming
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Intelligent reflecting surface (IRS) is a promising technology to enhance wireless communication networks. The IRS is heralded as a cost-effective, energy-efficient solution for extending the range and enhancing capacity of the wireless systems. The main premise of the IRS is that it can impart controlled phase offsets to the multiple replicas of the transmitted signal such that they arrive phase coherently at the destination. In this paper, we propose a deep-learning (DL) based approach for an IRS-aided return link beamformer. Our proposal determines both the IRS phase shifts as well as the receiver-side beamforming coefficients. The Deep Neural Network (DNN) that we deploy directly generates the quantized form of the IRS phase coefficients that can be directly used at the IRS thereby jointly solving the problems of coefficient determination and their quantization. We conduct experimental evaluation of our proposal and and show that our scheme is effective in solving the dual problems of determining the IRS phase shifts and the beamforming coefficients.

articleTitle: FSS based Wide Band and Polarization-Insensitive EM Wave Absorber for RCS Reduction Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper investigates an FSS-based, wide-band, polarization-insensitive, and lightweight EM wave absorber. The proposed design consists of four number of arrow shaped FSS patterns along with SMD resistors printed on 0.25 mm thin Duroid substrates. The top substrate is separated from the bottom side of the structure by an air spacer that is 5.5 millimeters thick. The bottom side of the structure is complete metal. The proposed design offered a wide absorption bandwidth of 14.9 GHz (5.8 - 20.7 GHz). The presented FSS unit cell has a surface area of 0.19λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Lg</inf> × 0.19λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Lg</inf> and a thickness of 0.108λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>, where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Lg</inf> is wavelength at 5.8 GHz. In this case, the thickness of the suggested structure is 5.6 millimeters, which is extremely close to the Razonov limit. The simulation results demonstrate that the designed FSS absorbs EM wave from 5.8 to 20.8 GHz band with angular stability of 50° for both polarizations. In addition to angular stability, the suggested design is polarization insensitive in the working band. The presented structure is also studied for its RCS, and to demonstrate its real time application in RCS reduction, the RCS (mono and bi-static) of the absorber structure is calculated and compared with the metal sheet’s RCS of the same size. Here, the absorption mechanism inside the proposed FSS is further exploited with the help of input impedance plot, E-field, and surface current distribution.

articleTitle: Design of Spiral Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper explains about a compact multiband single arm Archimedean spiral antenna with taper feed. The antenna is designed on a 1.57mm thick Roger’s RT Duroid 5880 substrate and it operates at 1.24GHz, 1.76GHz, 2.43GHz, 3.29GHz, 5.8Ghz with good impedance matching, Gain and Radiation pattern characteristics. The antenna would be very promising for vehicular communications which involve navigational wireless frequencies, wireless communication frequencies and dedicated short range communication frequency.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization of Compact multi band Metamaterial antenna using Machine Learning Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this article compact multi band meta material antenna by using split ring resonator concept is present and thoughtful attempt is made to introduce machine learning optimization for the designed antenna. The designed (10 X 10) mm compact multiband metamaterial antenna on FR-4 substrate (ɛ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> =4.4) using line feeding is working at 14.42GHz, 18.92GHz & 25.22GHz frequencies with operating bandwidth of 1820MHz, 340MHz & 960MHz and VSWR of 0.17dB, 2.82dB & 0.48dB, S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> of -40.04dB, -15.91dB -31.17dB respectively. Split ring resonator concept is used for the basic design in high frequency structural simulator for the multi band antenna design. The Machine Learning (ML) approach for the optimization of antenna is discussed at length. The output error and standard deviation for the standard ML model is discussed. The proposed antenna has potential applications at 5G frequencies with multiple band operation for GSM, high data rate transmission, body area networks and Tera hertz applications.

articleTitle: A Dual band 28GHz and 39GHz 4-port Vivaldi MIMO antenna for 5G wireless devices
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A novel compact dual band 4-port Vivaldi MIMO(Multiple Inputs Multi Outputs) antenna is designed for 5G wireless devices. Proposed antenna is resonate at two frequencies 28GHz and 39GHz and has dimensions 22x22x0.8mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. For proposed antenna Rogers RT/Duroid 5880 material is used having 0.8 thickness and 2.2 dielectric material. The bandwidths achieved for two bands are 4.64GHz (26.31-30.95GHz) at 28GHz resonant frequency, 2.69GHz (38.35- 41.04GHz) at 39GHz resonant frequency. The gain achieved at 28GHz is 5.65dB and at 39GHz is 5.53dB. It is possible to achieve MIMO performance parameters such ECC <0.001, DG = 10, CCL <0.4 (bits/s/Hz), TARC< -10dB, and MEG ratio is 1.01. The simulation tool ansys HFSS is used to design the antenna.

articleTitle: Design of Dual Band mm Wave Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) Antenna for Future Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a novel compact dual-band multiple input multiple output (MIMO) antenna is suggested for use in 5G mmWave wireless communication applications. The antenna of size 12 × 4.8 × 0.508 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> which is fed by a 50- microstrip feedline and is designed on Rogers RT/duroid 5880(tm) dielectric material. The proposed antenna comprises of a pair of orthogonally placed elements on top of sustrate and a slotted ground on bottom of substrate. On each radiating element, a rectangular slot was employed to produce resonance at the 28GHz band, which spans 27.5GHz to 28.6GHz. In order to obtain a second resonance at 48GHz between 46.6GHz and 49.1GHz, a couple of square slote were cut into the ground. The antenna offers good impedance matching at the working bands with S11<-10dB. The antenna elements arranged orthogonally to achieve isolation between the ports. To improve the isolation further, a narrow rectangular slot is used on the ground. The antenna provides high isolstion of >32dB, peak gains of 7.8dBi at 28GHz and 5.3dBi at 48GHz, radiation efficiencies of >90% at operating bands, omnidirectional radiation patterns, envelop correlation coefficient (ECC) of 0.0016, diversity gain (DG) of 10dB, total active reflection coefficient (TARC) of <-6dB, mean effective gain (MEG) of -3dB. The results manifests that the proposed design is good choice for 5G mmWave wireless communication applications.

articleTitle: Wideband Reconfigurable Linear-Linear and Linear-Circular Polarizer/Reflector Integrated With RF PIN Diodes for X/Ku/Ka-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This study demonstrates a reconfigurable wideband reflective polarizer from X to Ka-band applications. The design unitcell consists of a single PIN diode integrated metallic patch printed on a grounded dielectric substrate. When the PIN diode is reversely biased, the designed polarizer effectively converts a linearly polarized incident wave into a circular one with an effective 3 dB Axial Ratio (AR) from 8.88-9.82 GHz, 12.61-20.17 GHz, and 23.67-25.08 GHz. In addition, it also performs linear-cross conversion with a minimum 90% Polarization Conversion Ratio (PCR) from 10.43-11.68 GHz and 21.27-22.78 GHz. While in the forward bias, this polarizer behaves as a perfect reflector in the lower frequency region, linear-cross conversion (21.90-23.38 GHz), and linear-circular from 19.85-21.08 GHz and 24.44-26.77 GHz. No performance degradation for oblique incidences is observed in the elevation plane up to 45°. The dual functionality is due to several surface plasmonic resonances supported by the patterns seen in the local electric field. The polarizer/reflector unitcell is very compacted (0.053λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>×0.077 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>) and has a low-profile thickness of 0.047λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>. Dual operation is of paramount importance in real-time applications, and angular stable linear-cross, linear-circular polarizers and perfect reflectors at distinct frequency bands in a single design would be ideal in these cases.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Pascal Triangle Shaped Chip-less RFID Tag Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this article, the design of chip-less RFID tag antenna is presented. The chip-less RFID tag functions in frequency domain. The geometry of the tag is developed on FR4 epoxy substrate with footprint of 12.6 x 12.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The structure consists of a triangular open loop resonator loaded with micro-metallic patches of triangular shape. The tag can map 1-bit memory, used to encode one-bit, and its code density of 5.668 bits/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The analysis of RFID tag is discussed in terms of monostatic RCS configurations and also proposed the possible combinations with micro-metallic patches and analyzed in terms of RCS. The designer can use the available configuration for a wide range of modern applications.

articleTitle: High Gain Dual-Band Shorting Pins Loaded Microstrip Patch Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper proposes a high gain dual-band square-shaped microstrip patch antenna with the loading of two diagonally shorting pins. The radiation gain of the proposed square patch antenna for the first band is 7.06dBi at frequency 1.5GHz, while for the second band, it is -12.2dBi at frequency 3.05GHz. We propose a new method for improving the second band gain from -12.21 dBi to 10.1 dBi by placing two diagonally shorting pins. The impedance matching bandwidth (IMBW) for the first band is 3.3 %, while for the second band impedance matching bandwidth is 9.8 %. A systematic approach is proposed to identify the accurate position for loading the shorting pins in a square patch to enhance the gain of the second band. The gain of the proposed antenna in the first band is 7.06dBi, while for the second band, it is 10.1dBi.

articleTitle: Dual-Sense Polarized Dielectric Resonator Antenna with Metamaterial as Superstrate
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This work proposes a dual-sense rectangular dielectric resonator antenna (DRA) with dual-band response. The proposed DRA comprises a line feed and a metamaterial as a superstrate to achieve dual functional bands. Feeding is provided by using double conformal microstrip lines along the surface of DR material (ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> = 9.8) with 90 degrees in between the lines, forming an L-shaped patch etched on the dielectric substrate of FR-4 Epoxy (ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> = 4.4). The proposed antenna possesses two senses of polarization; i) a resonant frequency of 2.76GHz with linear sense polarization and ii) a resonant frequency of 3.36 GHz with a circular sense of polarization and an axial ratio bandwidth of 200 MHz (3.35-3.55 GHz). The gains obtained are 6dBi at 2.76 GHz and 4.6 dBic at 3.36 GHz.

articleTitle: EM Design and Analysis of FSS-based Composite Broadband Radar Absorbing Structure
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: EM design and performance analysis of FSS-based composite broadband radar absorbing structure (RAS) is presented in this paper. In this design hybrid FSS unit is used where square patch and cross dipole are arranged in the diagonal direction. The square patch resonates at lower frequency side while cross dipole resonates at higher frequency side that leads to broadband characteristics. The EM analysis of proposed FSS-RAS is carried out using commercial HFSS software. The total thickness of FSS-RAS is optimized to be 3.8 mm for better EM absorption characteristics. The proposed FSS-RAS is observed to exhibits broadband absorption characteristics from 6 GHz to 21.7 GHz w.r.t. -10 dB reflection loss. Moreover, the EM characteristics is found to be polarization independent up to 50° incidence angle. Such FSS-RAS can potentially be used over leading wing edge of aircraft to reduce its radar signature.

articleTitle: Impact of the Design Parameters on the Microwave Displacement Sensor Performance
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The investigations have been conducted on the involved design parameters to analyze the behavior of the microwave displacement sensor output characteristics. To implement this, a dielectric resonator loaded to a reflection mode operated microstrip line circuit is proposed. For the proposed reflection mode sensor, the sensor features like resonant frequency, impedance matching position, sensitivity, and dynamic range are sensitive to the displacement of DR to microstrip line. The impact of the substrate shape and size, and resonators geometrical properties are numerically analyzed and experimentally validated by using VNA. The sensor analysis shows good matching between both HFSS simulations and VNA measurements.

articleTitle: Design of Log Periodic Dielectric Resonator Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The proposed antenna is a broadband dielectric resonator fed via microstrip. Seven dielectric resonators, a microstrip feeding line, and a lumped port make up the antenna. The seven rectangular Dielectric resonators were placed next to each other on the microstrip feeding line in a log periodic arrangement. The matching bandwidth can be expanded using this method. The LPDRA is simulated on an FR4 epoxy substrate. The Reflection Coefficient is obtained for the frequency range of 11 to 18 GHz.

articleTitle: Hardware Simulator for FMCW Radar Altimeter
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Radar field performance verification is limited by test platform constraints such as operational range, velocity and acceleration. In order to verify system behaviour under different dynamic conditions, the hardware simulator systems are used that demonstrate a high degree of fidelity in the lab. This paper describes the hardware architecture of simulator based on high speed AD9850 frequency synthesizer. This has helped in verification of FPGA based data processing scheme and estimations in presence of artefacts due to dynamic conditions. Developed simulator has been evaluated in the lab under different dynamic conditions and the corresponding results have been summarized in this paper.

articleTitle: Ultra Miniaturised Wideband Linear-to-Circular and Linear-to-Cross Polarization Conversion Reflector with H-Dipole Loaded with Capacitive Patches
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A Frequency Selective Surface (FSS) based wideband reflective linear-cross and linear-circular polarization converter is proposed. The FSS consists of an H-shaped electric dipole loaded with capacitive patches printed on top of the low-loss dielectric spacer with the other side grounded. For the y/x linearly polarized wave incidence on the proposed design, the reflected wave is orthogonally polarized with a 90% Polarization Conversion Ratio (PCR) from 6.74-13.20 GHz, 15.96-17.20 GHz, and 23.78-26.44 GHz. It is not only limited to that but also performs linear-circular conversion with 3-dB minimum Axial Ratio (AR) from 3.36-5.18 GHz, 17.80-21.80 GHz, and 27.29-28.66 GHz. This design is highly miniaturized with a very compact structural periodicity of 0.034λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>×0.040 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> and a low-profile thickness of 0.018λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>, where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf> is the free-space wavelength of the lowest operating frequency. Considerable stable performance is achieved for different oblique incidences. The simulated surface current patterns are investigated for top FSS and ground for multiple resonant frequencies. The dual-polarized linear-cross and linear-circular polarizing reflectors in a single design with distinct frequency bands would be ideal for dual operation based real-time applications.

articleTitle: Ultrathin High Q-Factor Perfect Metamaterial Absorber for Sensing Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a simple ultrathin near-perfect metamaterial absorber with a high Q-factor in the microwave frequency range for refractive index sensing applications. The absorber is composed of an 8-point star ring with arrow extensions engraved over the grounded FR4 substrate. The designed absorber has an extended advantage of polarization stability and also has wide oblique incidence angle acceptance. The numerical simulation results reveal that the absorber has a narrow absorption band at the frequency of 4.62 GHz with an absorbance of 99.73%, and FWHM of 180 MHz. The Q-factor of this absorber is evaluated as 25.68 with average Sensitivity and average FoM of 0.47 GHz/RIU and 2.88, respectively. Herein, the absorbance of the designed absorber is also validated using the equivalent circuit modeling. The numerical analysis of the suggested absorber as a refractive index sensor shows enhanced parameters of sensitivity, linearity, and output variations, thus making this absorber a potential choice for various other sensor applications as well.

articleTitle: Novel Tunable Mixer Using Double Section Hybrid Coupler for Extended ISM Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a tunable mixer having a tunable range from 868 MHz to 2.4 GHz is proposed. The structure consists of a modified tunable 3 dB double section hybrid coupler along with a tunable 3<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">rd</sup> order low pass filter. The tunibility is achieved by varying the reverse biased voltage of the varactor diode. In the proposed circuit, only one control voltage is applied with RF choke inductors. For mixing operation, two schottky diodes are used. Working methodologies of the proposed mixer is established with extensive simulation results. Finally, proposed design gives wide tuning range, high port isolation, good return loss throughout the frequency range over 868 MHz to 2.4 GHz.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Geodetic Grade Antenna for GNSS & NavIC Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The design of a low cost multi band rectangular slot rectangular microstrip patch antenna (RSRMSA) & Defected ground structure (DGS) for GNSS (L1, L2, & L5) & NavIC (L5) application is presented. The paramount goal of this research is to design and optimize a RMSA for these three bands with a compact size and high performance which is suitable for above mentioned applications. RSRMSA resonates at L1, L2, & L5 bands of GNSS & NavIC applications. A general-purpose copper clad FR4 substrate is used for the proposed design to reduce the cost. The proposed patch antenna is fed by inset type microstrip line feed matched to 50Ω impedance. Miniaturization is obtained by etching slots into the radiating patch and ground plane. The proposed antenna resonates at L1 (1575.42 MHz), L2 (1227.6 MHz) & L5 (1176.45 MHz) with return loss of -16 dB, -20 dB & -35 dB respectively. It has measured VSWR ≤ 2 bandwidth of 37 MHz (2.34 %) in L1 band & 116 MHz (9.6%) including L2 & L5 band. The proposed work has a peak gain of 2dB in L2 & L5 band with good radiation pattern (RP). The designing and optimized results are obtained using Ansys HFSS antenna software. Various techniques such as slots, DGS are used to enhance antenna performance.

Author Keywords: Rectangular Slot Rectangular Microstrip Patch Antenna (RSRMSA)

articleTitle: On-Board Internal RF Calibration Electronics for Space-borne SAR
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents the design and measured results of On-board Internal RF Calibration Electronics comprising of a low power dissipation Calibration Switch Matrix realized using hermetically sealed MMIC based Single Pole Double Throw (SPDT) and Single Pole Single Throw (SPST) switches with coplanar waveguide with lower ground plane (CPWG) interconnects and calibration signal distribution network realized using RF power dividers for X-Band Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR). Calibration signal routing functionality for all antenna beam outputs, individual High Power Amplifier (HPA) outputs, individual Front-end Low Noise Amplifiers (LNA) of all antenna beams as well as the chirp (replica) has been realized by configuring a 3x2 Calibration Switch Matrix comprising of 2 inputs, 1 output and 1 bidirectional port. This multi-facet on board calibration scheme is required in SAR payloads to know the actual differential phase and amplitude variations across the transmit and receive modules, the actual imbalances of the antenna beams and having a reference chirp (replica) data required for pulse compression. The main and redundant switch matrix units are stacked with its respective Electronic Power Conditioning (EPC) unit and cross patching power dividers in a three-tier stack. Excellent isolation between desired and undesired signal along all paths has been achieved with the switches consuming a power of only 160mW. A low power dissipation, high isolation X-Band switch matrix, required for On-board Internal RF calibration electronics, has been designed, realized and successfully delivered for three satellite constellation of 8-beam reflector based SAR.

articleTitle: A Leaf Shaped Patch Antenna for Wideband Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper proposes a leaf-shaped patch antenna with a microstrip line printed on an FR-4 substrate. The overall antenna size is 26 X 27 X 1.6mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The impact of incorporating a Complementary Split Ring Resonator (CSRR) and Defected Ground Structure (DGS) on a Leaf shaped patch antenna is analyzed. Ultra-wideband with CP is obtained for the proposed design. Obtained bandwidth is 15GHz (4.12GHz to 19.12GHz), and the CP bandwidth is 290MHz with a peak gain of 6.44 dBi at 14.84 GHz. The proposed antenna is designed for UWB, C, X, and Ku bands. It is useful in Satellite and radar applications. Simulations are carried out using Ansys High-Frequency structure simulator.

articleTitle: Multi Mode (Reflection and Transmission) Operated Dielectric Resonator based Displacement Sensor
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A multi-mode operated microwave resonator based displacement sensor is presented. To enable this, a cylindrical dielectric resonator (DR) coupled microstrip line structure is established. The parameters like |S11| in reflection mode and |S21| in transmission mode are sensitive to DR displacements w.r.to transmission lines. The HFSS is carried out for numerical analysis and the fabricated sensor prototype is realized with VNA measurement. The sensor exhibits sensitivity of 6.2 dB/mm in the range of 0-4 mm in reflection mode and 1 dB/mm over 0-18 mm range in transmission mode. Both the HFSS and VNA responses are in good agreement with each other for this multi-mode operation. This reveals the selection of mode freedom to the choice of operation.

articleTitle: Single Feed Linearly and Circularly Polarized Dual Band Microstrip Patch Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A design of single feed, dual band and dual polarized microstrip patch antenna is presented here. The dual bands 2.2 GHz - 2.3 GHz and 2.7 GHz - 2.8 GHz with 63 MHz and 82 MHz bandwidth respectively, radiating at linear and circular polarizations. A single coaxial probe feed is used and design implemented in CST microwave studio. Resonant frequencies obtained at 2.23 GHz and 2.73 GHz with reflection coefficient of -32.32 dB for linear polarization in first band and -23.21 dB for circular polarization in second band. Circular polarization is achieved by trimming corners and diagonal feed point on patch.

articleTitle: Radiation Efficiency Improvement of a Microstrip Patch Antenna with a Lossy Substrate
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a cost-effective and simple technique of placing grounded metals next to the radiating edges of the patch antenna to improve the antenna’s radiation efficiency. The proposed technique is specifically for lossy substrate material. In this work, results are shown for a parametric sweep across a distance of the grounded metal to the antenna, frequency of operation, and loss tangent of the substrate to understand the behavior of the patch antenna with the grounded metal plates. The radiation efficiency is shown to improve up to 6% at 2.3 GHz of antenna operation.

articleTitle: Triple-band antenna for GPS, Sub-6 GHz 5G and WLAN Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A multi-band antenna based on rectangular patch, and split ring resonator shaped structure operates at 1.25 GHz, 3.55 GHz, and 5.28 GHz for GPS, Sub-6 GHz 5G and WLAN applications, respectively is proposed. The proposed antenna offers return loss of -21.07 dB, -22.44 dB, and -18.60 dB at the resonance with impedance bandwidth of 0.03 GHz, 0.05 GHz, and 0.29 GHz and VSWR of 1.19, 1.16, and 1.27 for desired applications bands, respectively. The proposed antenna offers a gain of 2.97 dBi, 5.36 dBi, and 4.87 dBi with a radiation efficiency of 42%, 94.7%, and 96.3% for intended bands, respectively. The proposed antenna is fed by a coaxial probe and physical dimension of 100×100×3.175 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> size. The antenna is designed on Rogers AD255C substrate. Characteristic mode analysis is carried out to identify radiating modes based on modal significance, characteristic angle, and eigenvalue. The reported antenna offers a linear polarized radiation patterns, simple structure, appropriate gain, and radiation efficiency making it suitable for desired applications for 5G enabled devices.

articleTitle: Compact Second and Third order Bandpass Filters based on QMSIW with Wide Fractional Bandwidth
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This work describes a class of compact bandpass filters (BPF) based on a quarter-mode substrate integrated waveguide (QMSIW) cavity. The benefit of using these filters is that they combine the features of SIW structures with improved size-reduction capabilities. First, a two-pole BPF is proposed featuring a quarter-mode SIW cavity with two orthogonal 50 Ω microstrip feedlines. The designed filter-I has the center frequency at 3.3 GHz with an insertion loss of 1.1 dB and a wide stopband of 2.23f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> with a minimum of 20 dB rejection level. It has a small footprint of $0.11\lambda _g^2$. Then, a three-pole BPF is achieved from filter-I by coupling it with an L-shaped microstrip line. The filter-II has the center frequency at 3.1 GHz with an insertion loss of 1.82 dB and a wide stopband of 1.9f<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> with a minimum of 20 dB rejection level. The footprint of the filter-II remains almost the same. The proposed QMSIW filters are suitable for WiMAX applications due to their compact size, planar structure, and adequate bandwidth.

articleTitle: Energy Harvesting Antenna from Wi-Fi, WiMAX and ISM Bands
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents the energy harvesting antenna with a 1×2 array. The wearable patch array antenna design is illustrated using electro textile materials. Patch array antenna simulations have been conducted using several different materials, including Copper Polyester Taffeta, Shielded Super, and Copper. Because of their low loss tangent and high dielectric constant, jeans is used as the substrate, increasing bandwidth and reducing power loss. Also, compare the simulated and measured array antenna with copper polyester taffeta material. Analyzing the results, it is found that the copper polyester taffeta array antenna provides adequate results good impedance matching network. So, it can be used for energy harvesting application from Wi-Fi, WiMAX, and ISM bands.

articleTitle: A Low Profile CDRA with Tapered Feed for UWB Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A low profile quadrilateral-shaped patch-fed Cylindrical Dielectric Resonator Antenna (CDRA) for Ultra Wideband (UWB) applications is presented in this paper. The antenna structure employs a 50-Ω tapered feed line with the modified ground plane. Greater bandwidth and improved impedance matching are provided by a modified ground plane. The patch is loaded with a CDRA in order to get a wideband performance. TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01δ</inf> modes are observed at both frequencies of 4.6 GHz and 11.2 GHz. The proposed CDRA offers UWB of 116% from 3.4 GHz to 12.8 GHz. A peak gain of 5.76 dBi is reached at 12.2 GHz. At lower frequencies antenna shows an omnidirectional radiation pattern. The proposed CDRA has also a low profile of 0.02 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the lower cut-off frequency wavelength.

articleTitle: NISAR S-SAR Multichannel Receive chain ground characterization
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: ISRO and JPL(NASA) are developing a synthetic aperture radar (SAR) mission to map Earth's surface every 12 days, known as NASA-ISRO SAR (NISAR). NISAR is based on novel SweepSAR concept to provide wider swath along with high spatial resolution <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[6] & [7]</sup>. It uses a large deployable reflector antenna with a phased array antenna feed. To illuminate wider swath during transmit, all feed elements are excited to sub-illuminate reflector. While on receive, a much smaller portion of phased array antenna is used to collect the return echo. As per the joint agreement, JPL (NASA) is developing the L-Band SAR and ISRO is developing the S-Band SAR <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">[6]</sup>. S-SAR employs scan on receive with digital beamforming (DBF) and has 48 receiver chains (24H+24V Pol). In this paper, end to end characterization of integrated receive chain is presented. The paper focuses on measurement techniques, challenges and test methodologies used to characterize the multiple receiver chains. The measurement results and their compliance with payload performance specifications has been discussed.

articleTitle: Design of Cavity-backed Coaxial Ring Slot Antenna for Dual-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a coaxial ring slot antenna with a cavity backing using substrate-integrated waveguide (SIW) technology. This antenna consists of rectangular and circular SIW cavities each having a circular ring slot on the top conductor of the antenna. A coaxial feed is used to feed circular cavity which is inserted into the rectangular cavity fed with inset microstrip feed. With the slot antenna radiators size suitably optimized in the two cavities, a small frequency ratio is achieved between the two bands. The proposed antenna has been designed to radiate two different frequencies at 5.36GHz and 5.76GHz. Good radiation pattern characteristics are achieved which are unidirectional and have a stable gain of 3.6dBi at the resonance frequencies. Further, the antenna is easy to realize and is very compact. The measured results are found to be in good arrangement with simulation result.

articleTitle: 3D Printed Multiple Hexagonal Ring Radiator Flexible Antenna for WLAN and 5G Millimeter Wave Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A new type of 3D flexible multiband antenna is proposed for use in wireless local area networks (WLAN) and fifth generation (5G) millimeter wave (mmWave) applications. The proposed antenna is built on a Ninjaflex substrate and consists of multiple hexagonal ring radiators with decreasing diameter when viewed from top to bottom. This unique 3D structure and microstrip feeding technique allows the proposed antenna to operate at resonant frequencies of 5.70 GHz, 27.30 GHz, and 34.30 GHz, meeting the -10 dB impedance bandwidth for WLAN and 5G mmWave frequency bands. Simulated results also show that the proposed antenna demonstrates good radiation performance in terms of power patterns, radiation efficiency, and gain across all three resonant frequencies.

articleTitle: Realization of Planar Array Antenna for SAR Application using Brush Plating
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Mechanical design of antenna has been carried out in order to cater for realization of 1.4m long micro strip feed line as a single component, eliminating deficiencies associated with RF interconnections on PCB based planar antenna. Selection of metal was done in such a way that it should be less prone to corrosion and sustained in a long way as well as low cost. The antenna patches, feed probes & micro strip feedline is made up of Al6061-T6. It is required to protect the exposed surfaces of feedline from corrosion and oxides formation, while maintaining surface electrical conductivity. Solderability of the feed line at connector feed locations is also required in order to form a good solder joint between connector and feed line. Keeping in view the size of feed line (1.4m X 0.3m X 0.002m) and also the cost involved in silver plating entire feed, a need of selective, local silver plating process is felt, which can improve the solderability of aluminum feed line at selective locations only and remaining area of feed line is chromated to provide required corrosion resistance and surface electrical conductivity. Brush silver plating process is evolved which has been recently developed, has been successfully used for doing selective plating on complex and difficult to handle job. It is successfully implemented to yield desired conductivity for RF use.

articleTitle: High Frequency Integrated Microwave Circuit Board Designed for the X-band Signal Generation
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A novel technique for the implementation of single board high frequency RF and Microwave subsystems for frequency generators is demonstrated through the X-band signal generation. This paper explains how high frequency RF and Microwave circuits viz. Amplifiers, Multipliers, Mixers, Modulators, Band pass filters and Low pass filters can be integrated on the single board and the board can be used for the the high frequency, miniaturized RF and Microwave subsystem after the successful design and development.

articleTitle: 3-D Manufactured Antenna Hardware for Space and Ground Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: 3D printing technology has made significant advances in recent times enabling feeds and antennas to be manufactured meeting high performance requirements for space and ground applications. This paper presents 3-D manufactured antenna hardware using both metals and plastics. Several antenna designs and hardware are discussed along with their RF performance and photographs.

articleTitle: High Efficiency Broadband Class F Power Amplifier for Sub-6-GHz 5G Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a performance analysis of the high efficiency broadband Class F Power Amplifier using even-odd mode matching techniques in Gallium Nitride HEMT Technology for Sub-6-GHz 5G Application. The proposed design circuit consists of broadband input matching network which provides a wideband operation by canceling higher harmonics, high efficiency Class F main amplifier, and series shunt network to enhance the bandwidth. The proposed PA with built-in techniques achieves a fractional impedance bandwidth of 110% in frequency range 2 GHz to 5GHz. The GaN HEMT PA is analyzed and simulated using Keysight’s Advanced Design System simulator. A maximum drain efficiency of 78.82% is achieved with a power gain ranging from 10~14 dBm. In addition, an output power > 40 dBm is achieved with the proposed design with drain voltage of 28 V.

articleTitle: High Gain Dual Polarized Antenna System for STAR Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a novel simultaneous transmit and receive (STAR) antenna system operating around 3.5 GHz with high gain, high isolation and low cross polarization. The designed dual polarized antenna is a multi-layer planar patch antenna, and is differentially excited with a pair of wideband planar baluns. This differential feeding scheme not only reduces the self-interference but also helps in improving the isolation between the differential ports. The defected ground structures (DGS) underneath the patch are used to enhance of antenna bandwidth. The simulated |S11| ≤ - 10 dB bandwidth is 100 MHz, isolation is better than 59 dB while realized gain is 10.1 dBi at Tx port while it is 9.34 dBi at the Rx port. The total efficiency is better than 80 % for both the ports.

articleTitle: Phase Corrected Substrate Integrated Waveguide H-Plane Horn Antenna with Dielectric Loading
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The phase distribution of the electromagnetic field in the horn antenna is usually not uniform throughout the horn aperture, resulting in a lower gain. In this paper, the concept of phase correction, along with impedance matching, is presented. A coaxial-fed, Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) based H plane horn antenna is proposed for the X band. The SIW horn antenna is splitted into three sub-horn structures for phase correction by etching slots on the horn surface. To improve impedance matching extended substrate is used. The overall size of the proposed antenna is 51×40×0.79 mm3, designed on RT- duroid 5880. The proposed antenna is compact having a maximum gain of 8.1 dB, whereas the maximum gain of a traditional horn antenna is 0.597 dB.

articleTitle: Dual Circularly Polarized Aperture Coupled Patch Antenna for Diversity Reception
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A dual-port dual circularly polarized aperture coupled patch antenna designed for S-band telemetry application is presented in this paper. A microstrip line quadrature hybrid is used as the feed to excite two orthogonal modes of the patch. An H-shaped slot is used to couple fields to the patch antenna. An air dielectric of 6mm thickness is used between the patch and the quadrature hybrid feed to achieve a broad bandwidth. The antenna is having a 2:1 VSWR bandwidth of 22% centered at 2.25GHz, axial ratio bandwidth of 10%, and 1dBi gain variation within 7.5% bandwidth with a peak gain of 7.8dBi. The antenna is RHCP/LHCP polarized when excited from respective ports with an axial ratio of less than 3dB. The overall dimension of the antenna is 75mm x 75mm x 7.5mm.

articleTitle: DC-5 GHz GaAs HEMT Absorptive SP4T Switch
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: An absorptive single pole four throw (SP4T) broadband MMIC switch is designed using the PE15 GaAs HEMT process of WIN foundry. The designed switch has inbuilt decoder and driver circuitry. This MMIC process has both depletion as well as enhancement (0.5 μm) FET capability where depletion mode FET is used for the design of RF switches while depletion and enhancement mode is used for the design of decoder and its driver circuitry to minimize power consumption. The assembled switch provides greater than 25 dB isolation and less than 2.8 dB insertion loss up to 5 GHz. The return losses are better than 11.5 dB over the entire frequency range and works with the control voltage of 0 and 5V. The switch is realized within the footprint of 3.5mm x 2.5mm x 0.1mm and consumes only 75mW of power.

articleTitle: Gap waveguide Technology Based Transmission Lines at V Band and W Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents new metamaterial based gap waveguide transmission lines referred to as ridge, groove gap waveguide for millimeter-wave applications. The gap waveguides have lower losses than microstrip lines, Moreover they are completely shielded by metal so that no additional packaging is needed, in contrast to the severe packaging problems associated with conventional waveguides. Ridge and groove gap waveguides are studied by characterizing the S parameters of each structure in V band and W band frequency range. Further, the losses in both structures is analyzed. These transmission line structures would be very promising in designing the magic tee, couplers, power dividers, antenna etc., for mm wave communication systems.

articleTitle: Ultra-Wide Band Semi-elliptical antenna for MIMO Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Ultra-Wide Band (UWB) systems can support high data rate transmission because of which they are in demand in several applications and have brought challenges in antenna design. When compared to common narrow-band antennas UWB antennas are cheap, have low power consumption, good effectively, and achieve broad bandwidth. In this paper, a four-element semi-elliptical UWB MIMO antenna is designed for wireless applications. The MIMO antenna is printed on a low-cost FR-4 Epoxy substrate of size 52 × 48 × 1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and is fed by an asymmetric coplanar strip (ACS) lin. The proposed antenna radiates across 3 GHz to 12 GHz frequency range. It has good reflection coefficient characteristics and it generates an acceptable omnidirectional radiation pattern, with a peak gain of 3.7 dBi at 8 GHz. Good performance in diversity gain, and Envelope Correlation Coefficient (ECC), which is suitable for MIMO applications is achieved.

articleTitle: Lightning Electromagnetic Simulation through Streamer Discharge
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The focus of this paper is to validate a simulation-based method for observing the growth and formation of streamers in nanosecond discharges under ambient conditions. The approach utilized in this study allows for an in-depth investigation of streamer behavior, providing valuable insights into the underlying mechanisms involved in the process. Discharge initiation and propagation between the tips of two needles are handled using the so-called drift model, which accounts for the electron losses, production, and movement. The same applies to the positive and negative ions. The development of secondary electrons at the head of the streamer as a result of photoionization is incorporated to model the spread of a streamer channel. This work reports on simulation of lightning strike through streamer using the commercial software COMSOL which replicates a streamer system having two electrodes that develop impulsive voltage at the central region of the electrodes, which in turn replicates the impulsive voltage of a spark. The simulation’s findings show that two streamers move in the direction towards each other in the air gap and that the discharge starts in regions with strong electrostatic fields which is closer to the edged curve part of the electrodes. Overall, this research provides a valuable contribution to our understanding of streamer formation and growth in nanosecond discharges at ambient conditions, and the findings of the simulation can be useful in designing and optimizing lightning protection systems.

articleTitle: Design of a Dual-Band Square Patch Antenna with L- Shaped Stubs and DGS for C & X-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper proposes a dual-band square patch antenna with four L-shaped stubs with the dimensions of a proposed antenna 54mm×54mm×1.6mm at the operating frequency is 6.8GHz. The square patch antenna with four L-shaped stubs results in a dual-band operation operating in a bandwidth of 810 MHz (7.27GHz to 7.44GHz) and 510MHz (9.70GHz to 9.86GHz) with a peak gain of 1.9dBi at 7.37GHz. To further improve the bandwidth (BW) and peak gain (dBi) the DGS is incorporated. With the incorporation of DGS, a bandwidth of 410MHz (6.29GHz to 6.7GHz) and 710MHz (11.03GHz to 11.74GHz) is obtained with a peak gain of a 3.51dBi at 6.5GHz and 5.79dBi at 11.34GHz. The proposed antenna with DGS is suitable for C & X-band applications. Simulations were carried out using ANSYS HFSS software.

articleTitle: Decision-Tree Based Machine Learning Approach for the Design and Optimization of 5G n78 Sub-Band Antenna for WiMAX/WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In these days, it is inevitable to apply the machine learning techniques in all fields of science and engineering including electromagnetic applications. In this article a thoughtful attempt is made to introduce decision tree machine learning algorithm for the design of a microstrip patch antenna for wireless WiMAX/WLAN application at 5G-n78 sub-band frequency (3.3GHz).The proposed antenna is a simple rectangular patch of 0.304λ X 0.238λ dimensions designed on FR-4 substrate (ɛ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> =4.4) by using line feeding technique. The antenna is radiating at 3.3GHz frequency with S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> of -37.4dB, VSWR of 0.233 and gain of 4.06 dB. The data points were collected from the full wave electromagnetic solver High Frequency Structural Simulator (HFSS) and decision tree is built in R-language platform. The decision tree algorithm is applied for multiple length values of metal patch by targeting S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11.</inf> The mean square error calculated is 3.459 & 3.75 for train and test data respectively, further decision tree is generated. The designed antenna has good potential to apply for wireless WiMAX/WLAN and 5G applications and the decision tree obtained is better suiting for the optimization of the designed antenna.

articleTitle: One-Dimensional Radiation Beam Tilting Using Thin Planner Phase Gradient Metasurfaces Array Lens at millimeter-Wave Band for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a thin planner metasurface (MS) lens technique is reported to deflect the radiation beam in predetermined direction at mm-Wave band for 5G applications. The MS lens array consists of phase gradient unit cells which capable to manipulates the phase of the incoming wave and transformed into the tilted beam. The unit cell has a square ring resonator and cross bar slots. The gradient phase is achieved by controlling the length of the square ring resonator slot. The total phase variation by tuning the length of the resonator is achieved 217<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> at 28 GHz. To check the authenticity of tilted radiation beam, the phase gradient metasurfaces (PGMS) array lens is fed by a conventional microstrip patch antenna. The patch antenna covers 27.5 – 28.5 GHz band with realized gain of 7.9 dBi at 28 GHz. The MS lens is loaded in the main radiation beam direction of the patch antenna i.e., at the top side. With this, the radiation beam is tilting ≈ 21<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sup> from the original radiation beam direction. Moreover, the MS array confined the radiation beam as a result the gain of the patch antenna is significantly increased about 2.17 dBi at 28 GHz.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of UHF Passive Dipole Antennas for Moisture Detection using RFID technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: RFID technology is taking over the market of sensor applications in the medical and healthcare industry. Radio frequency identification (RFID) tags are cost-effective and have better performance than other sensor applications. In this paper, we propose UHF passive antennas for moisture detection which can be used in the medical and healthcare industries. Dipole antennas working in UHF which has omnidirectional radiation patterns are designed and fabricated using RFID chip NXP UCODE G2iL SOT886 in the SMILE research lab which is tested in a different environments for the detection of moisture. Based on the antenna parameters the dry state and wet state of the environment is differentiated. The performance and results of dipole antennas like a meander dipole antenna, folded dipole antenna with closed loop and T-matched dipole antennas are compared and discussed in this paper. The dipole antennas are designed using HFSS simulation software at 866 MHz to achieve the antenna impedance of 25 + j237 ohms which is the complex conjugate of the load impedance. From the simulation and experimental results, it is found that the T-Matched dipole antenna has better antenna performance in terms of read range and detecting the moisture in the environment.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Ku-Band STALO for low phase noise applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Radar systems have largely adopted STALO local-oscillator (LO) generator for up/down conversions in TR modules. This paper describes an overview of Ku band Stable LO generation for the Transmitter and Receiver system with Low phase noise application. The LO chain Generates 15.375 GHz signal for up/down conversion. So, here the highly stable OCXO of 125 MHz is used as a reference signal to derive LO (Ku-band) signal and it is synthesized using LMX2615 Frequency synthesizer with OCXO frequency as a Reference clock signal followed by Frequency doubler for Upconversion of the LMX2615 output frequency. In the process of generation of LO chain, microstrip filters have been used that is the coupled line filter because of their good coupling gap and also wiggy coupler has been used for better isolation and directivity response which has been designed. The system typically needs LO with a specification of 0.5 dbm, low phase noise of -80 dBc/Hz @ 100 Hz offset, LO spurious, and harmonic rejection of <-60 dBc.

articleTitle: Highly Stable Frequency Selective Surface with Bandstop Characteristics for EMI Shielding for 28 GHz Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: For 28 GHz millimeter-wave (mm-wave) electromagnetic interference (EMI) shielding applications, a bandstop frequency selective surface (FSS) design is proposed. The proposed FSS design consists of a meandered square-loop element and a parasitic ring. The meandered square loop is designed to get resonance in the desired frequency band, while the parasitic element is utilized to tune the response at 28 GHz. According to the results, the optimized FSS resonates for the 28 GHz frequency band, with a bandwidth of 10.175 GHz (25.4-35.575 GHz). Additionally, the proposed FSS’s stability study is conducted, and it is found to offer a stable response for both TE and TM polarizations up to 60° oblique incidence. In addition, the shielding effectiveness (SE) of the proposed FSS is evaluated, and reasonable results are observed.

articleTitle: Millimeter-wave open resonator-based dielectric characterization of printed circuit boards
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this work, a low-permittivity polymer rod-based open-resonator has been demonstrated for the dielectric characterization of some commonly used printed circuit board substrates at K<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf>-band (26.5 GHz to 40 GHz). The concept of Fabry-Perot has been adapted at millimeter-wave frequency while ensuring a low-cost and robust design. First, the dielectric parameters and possible dielectric dispersion of the dielectric rod waveguide used in the open-resonator are investigated. This is done by fitting full-wave electromagnetic simulation results to the measured response. It is followed by introducing the test substrates into the resonant cavity of the open-resonator, thereby leading to an electromagnetic perturbation of the resonances. Finally, the dielectric parameters are extracted from the measured resonance frequency shifts for different test substrates. A wide range of relative permittivity is tested in the proposed setup, which features repeatability, considerable sensitivity to dielectric parameters, and relaxed assembly tolerances.

articleTitle: Index Modulation with Space Domain Coding
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Index Modulation (IM), and its variants, such as Space Shift Keying (SSK) and Spatial Modulation (SM), have been proposed for the next-generation wireless systems and are shown to provide high spectral/energy efficiencies and low implementation complexity. These systems utilize extra dimensions (e.g., spatial dimension), in addition to the conventional time/frequency dimensions, for information transmission. A simple Maximum Receive Ratio Combining (MRRC) based detector has been shown to be applicable for the IM decoding; however, it exhibits a significantly high antenna index detection error floor in the Rayleigh fading Multiple Input Multiple Output (MIMO) channels. Alternate schemes based on Maximum Likelihood (ML), Sphere Decoding (SD), or Hybrid Decoding (HD) reduce this error floor but at the cost of higher implementation complexity. This paper addresses reducing the antenna detection error in IM systems by proposing several new spatial domain forward error correction (FEC) schemes. In our first proposal, that we call Parity based SM (Pb-SM), the SM receiver uses the transmitted parity bits — sent via the modulated symbol on the selected transmit antenna — to estimate the antenna index. In the second proposal, that we call Antenna Encoding (AE), we form cosets of the transmit antennas (based either on the cross-correlation metric or on the Euclidean distance between the MIMO channel vectors) and use the coset index for information transfer. A simulation-based study presented in this paper demonstrates the effectiveness of the proposed schemes in reducing antenna detection errors.

articleTitle: CPW-Fed Multiband CRLH Antenna for GPS, ISM and 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A coplanar waveguide-fed multiband composite right/left-handed (CRLH) antenna, a class of metamaterials (MTMs) is presented in this paper. It is designed by embedding two unit-cells of CRLH transmission line on the top and bottom surfaces of an FR4 epoxy substrate with the help of metallic vias. The multiband characteristic is obtained by generating four resonances due to CRLH unit-cells, feed-patch and the ground plane. The simulated results show three frequency bands spanning over 1.3 to 1.87 GHz, 2.36 to 2.63 GHz and 3.14 to 4.62 GHz with return loss below – 10 dB. The realized gains have been found as 2.5, 2.56, 4.85 and 4.9 dB at the resonant frequencies of 1.57, 2.4, 3.4 and 4.2 GHz respectively. The radiation efficiency is well above 77% at each resonant frequency with a peak value of 94.76%. The proposed antenna is suitable for Global Positioning System (GPS) (1.57 GHz), Industrial, Scientific and Medical (ISM) (2.4 GHz), and 5G sub-6 GHz infrastructure (3.3-4.2 GHz) applications.

articleTitle: Bandwidth Reconfigurable Wideband Antenna with comparison between PIN diodes and Vanadium Dioxide switches
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A wideband microstrip patch antenna design is proposed in this paper having resonant frequency at around 5GHz and capability of bandwidth reconfiguration. The proposed design is a compact bidirectional wideband antenna having wideband starting frequency at around 5GHz and keeping the design simple, provides a high reconfigurability of bandwidth from 0.8GHz to 3.63GHz as the states of the antenna are switched. In this design only two PIN diodes are used to achieve bandwidth reconfiguration and the same design is also tested by replacing the PIN diodes with Vanadium dioxide(VO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>) switches to check their compatibility with the designed antenna and see if same results could be achieved with the same.

articleTitle: Planar frequency reconfigurable antenna for ISM/WiMAX applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A frequency reconfigurable antenna is proposed in this paper for ISM (Industrial, Scientific, and Medical) and WiMAX (Worldwide Interoperability for Microwave Access) applications. The suggested radiating monopole is in the shape of an F. With an overall small dimension of 30×33×1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>, this structure resonates in two separate states, at 2.4 GHz and 3.5 GHz. Placing a PIN diode at optimal points on the F shape allows you to switch between these bands.

articleTitle: Design of Single Feed Compact Circularly Polarized Dual Band Dielectric Resonator Antenna for L5 and S Bands Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this article, A dual-band circularly polarized, compact dielectric resonator antenna with high isolation, high gain has been introduced. The proposed antenna has realized circularly polarized radiation by applying asymmetrical cross slots embedded at the ground layer and balanced strip feed. From the circularly polarized radiation pattern, the cylindrical shape dielectric resonator antenna, when excited on its broadside, confirmed the HEM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11δ</inf> at 1.176 GHz (L5 band) and higher mode TM<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">01δ</inf> at 2.492 GHz (S band). Maximum of 3.06 dB and 6.05 dB circularly polarized gain have been achieved over axial ratio bandwidth of 16 MHz and 106 MHz in L5 and S bands. The achieved front-to-back ratio of 4.98 dB & 13.36 dB and cross polarization of -23.75 dB and -22.76 dB in L5 and S bands respectively appear quite satisfactory.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Coordinated Multipoint NOMA Cellular Networks
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: 5G cellular networks are expected to provide higher spectral efficiency and seamless connectivity to every subscriber. Non-Orthogonal Multiple Access (NOMA) is a promising technique to increase spectral efficiency and accommodate more cellular users. The cellular users near to the base station are always connected to the network due to the strong signal strength whereas users far from the base station suffer from poor signal reception. In order to mitigate this problem, in this paper, a coordinated multi-point NOMA cellular network with multiple cell edge-users is considered. In this system model, a practical scenario in which edge-users coordinate with two base stations is considered and nearby users are connected with the respective base station. The performance metrics such as outage probability and system capacity are derived for this system model. In addition, an algorithm has been proposed for the Nakagami-m fading channel to find these performance metrics by simulations. Numerical results show that the outage performance and data rate of the cellular users are better in the proposed coordinated system than the conventional uncoordinated system.

articleTitle: Preliminary Simulation and Experimental Studies on View Dump made of Silicon Carbide for Vertical Electron Cyclotron Emission Experiment
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper describes the simulation and experimental studies for the design and characterization of high-temperature and high vacuum compatible view dump; required to reduce the effects of scattering and tokamak wall reflections for the Vertical Electron Cyclotron Emission (VECE) diagnostic. Based on the in-vessel requirements, the silicon carbide (SiC) material is selected and the electromagnetic (EM) behavior of the slab and pyramid geometry fabricated from it is investigated. Firstly, simulations are performed to investigate the slab geometry and then modified into a pyramidal geometry to improve its absorption capabilities. To validate the simulation results, experiments are performed in the frequency range of 60–110 GHz.

articleTitle: Small Compact Folded Loop Antenna Feed for Wide Band Reflector Antennas
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A small compact feed antenna has been designed to meet the need for a 2 to 14 GHz frequency of operation for a reflector antenna. The feed has a nearly constant gain of 11dBi up to 10GHz and a slight drop of 1dB at higher bands 10 to 14 GHz. The broad beam, essentially constant gain, a small variation of phase center, and small cross-polarization of the feed make it suitable for a wideband reflector antenna system. The step-wise novel, a simple design method for such a large bandwidth-fed antenna, has been discussed, and simulated results of gain cross-polarization and return loss are presented.

articleTitle: In-band Multi-Channel Communication employing Multi-tone Time Modulated Array
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The future technologies modern era requisite a massive number of channels for communication. The design of an efficient and suitable antenna radiating multichannel within a band frequency is presented in this paper. First, multichannel radiation is established utilizing multi-tone radiation from the time-modulated array. Then, the multi-tone transmitter is designed by employing the optimized time modulation on the antenna array to generate multiple radiating beams with enhanced power. The optimization is conducted utilizing Harmony Search. The presented results convey that the optimized system radiates the multiple beams with sufficient power to accommodate multichannel communication to establish a smart environment.

articleTitle: Low Profile High Directive Configurable-circular polarised Antenna for C-Band Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a design of a high directive C-band Electro-Magnetically Coupled Patch (EMCP) antenna array fed with a 1×6 series power divider, exhibiting circular polarization properties. The proposed antenna array shows a good axial ratio and impedance bandwidth from 5.7 GHz to 5.9 GHz. The proposed antenna is compact, simple and occupies less printed circuit area. Furthermore, the design is simulated using commercially available electromagnetic software ANSYS. In addition, the array antenna is fabricated and measured with a gain of 15dBi with an axial ratio of less than 3 dB across the frequency band. It is observed that the measured performances are closely matches to simulated performances.

articleTitle: An application of the dimensionality reduction methods for contrast target detection in microwave imaging
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Microwave imaging systems have the capability to see through an optically opaque surface. Ground penetrating radar is a very popular application of microwave imaging that detects buried objects, and it is useful for defense and civilian applications. The scattered signal from the hidden object depends on the dielectric contrast between the object and the surrounding environment.
