In this regard, if the target with higher dielectric constant is present in the vicinity of the lower one, the detection becomes a challenging task for the lower dielectric constant target. This paper proposes a technique using dimensionality reduction to detect the targets with dielectric contrast efficiently. The results highlight the detection of multiple targets with dielectric contrast in a single scanning area.

articleTitle: Cross-Polarization Mitigation Technique in Vertically Integrable Antenna Elements for Phased Array Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This article presents mitigation techniques for cross-polarization in the vertically integrable antenna elements with wider half power beamwidth (HPBW). The phased array antennas (PAAs) requires wide band and wide HPBW antenna elements for construction to satisfy the wide scanning requirements over a wider operational bandwidth. Tapered slot antenna (TSA) satisfies these requirements but suffers from high cross polarization (CP) due to their high profile. The longer taper profile of these antennas facilitate surface currents to follow longer trajectory which leads to high level of cross polarization. This article deliberates upon the mitigation of CP and present some design techniques which modifies the taper profile with some groves to satisfy the above-cited requirements for PAA applications.

articleTitle: A Paradigm Shift in Exhaustive BIT Information and BIT Collection Mechanism over IP network for large Active Array Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Periodic checking of health status for any system or sub-system is of paramount importance in Active Array Aperture Antennas. This is accomplished by reporting and presenting to the user the Built-In Test (BIT) information. But till date the amount of information that is presented as BIT is modest and insufficient for exhaustive analysis and troubleshooting. In this paper we present a novel scheme of exhaustive BIT collection for a system. Apart from the traditional Central BIT or CBIT, the collection of Power-On BIT or PBIT and Initiated BIT or IBIT presents a comprehensive picture of Active Array Antenna Unit (AAAU) at any instant. Since the Line Replaceable Units (LRUs) are over Ethernet Internet Protocol (IP) network, hence the properties of IP network are thoroughly used to advantage for BIT collection Secondly, given that the number of LRUs are in tens of thousands, hence it becomes necessary to sequence the BIT collection mechanism with respect to time and at the same time sufficient care must be taken to the fact that the BIT collection time should be kept as minimal as possible. We address all these challenges in our current design of BIT collection. The architecture is scalable and can be easily adapted to large aperture arrays.

articleTitle: Frequency selective surface based radio frequency absorber at 90GHz of operational frequency
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Frequency ranging from 0.3GHz to 300GHz in Electromagnetic (EM) waves are known as Microwaves, for these wave the wavelengths use to be of the order of 1m to 1mm. These waves obeys all the laws of optics like reflection, absorption and refraction depending upon the boundary conditions of two mediums. Most of the time it is needed to absorb the EM waves to avoid the reflections in the DUT test zones. As per the available literature, EM wave absorbers can be designed & developed either using dielectric materials like carbon impregnated foam or using frequency selective surfaces (FSS). Foam based absorbers works on the principal of absorbing the incident EM wave and converting these EM energy into heat. Absorbers can provide two different type of losses i.e. electric loss and magnetic loss. Type of loss provided by absorbers depends upon the dielectric properties whether it is complex permittivity or complex permeability. Compact size of the absorbers can be achieved by using material with high value of permeability which can be achieved from ferrite or magnetic absorbers, but it can be achieved after pledging notable amount of time and resources A frequency-selective surface (FSS) is any papery, unvaried surface designed to follow the laws of optics to EM waves depending upon frequency, polarization, and angle of incidence. FSS resonating unvaried periodic array which depends upon the polarization, Angle of incidence and frequency of EM wave.In past decennium, a notable number of works and studies has been performed to work out the development of FSS surfaces. This area is still active to develop the structure that can control the indenting EM waves and provide a good amount of absorption to them.This paper presents a proof of concept demonstrating the efficient designing technique with minimum time and fabrication complexity & challenges. This concept shows the model produces a simple structure and provide around 90% RF Absorption at 90GHz of operational frequency.

articleTitle: Tri-band MIMO Diversity Antenna for Modern Smartphones
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper proposes the design of a MIMO antenna system with four elements, specifically tailored for future smartphones. The MIMO antenna system is operating in three important 5G frequency bands: 3.5 GHz, 4.7 GHz, and 5.8 GHz. The MIMO system utilizes a single hybrid H-shaped patch radiator as the radiating element, which is integrated into the smartphone’s side-edge frame. The main board of the device consists of the feeding lines. By employing this configuration, the antenna achieves a tri-band response, satisfying the -6 dB impedance bandwidth criteria for each desired frequency band, providing bandwidths of 680 MHz, 440 MHz, and 470 MHz, respectively. The MIMO antenna system also demonstrates notable performance characteristics, including a peak gain of 5.8 dBi, a radiation efficiency of 70%, and a total efficiency of 80%. The strategic placement of antenna elements at the corners of the side-edge frames ensures isolation of greater than 16 dB between the elements in the relevant frequency bands. Furthermore, this antenna design facilitates both spatial and pattern diversity, enhancing the overall performance of the MIMO system.

articleTitle: A Compact Rectangular Meander Slot and Antipodal Vivaldi radiator for 5G FR-II Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A resonator antenna constructed with a small rectangular meander line and antipodal vivadi left (AVL) for an integrated 5G frequency range-II (FR-II) is proposed in this study. The antenna’s W×L dimensions are 30mm × 22mm. FR4 epoxy, with a thickness of 1.6 mm, serves as the substrate material. The wideband is attained by establishing AVL and a slot in the resonator. Four rectangular slots are formed in the patch to make a two U shaped meander line. The calculated impedance bandwidth for the proposed architecture is 4.37GHz. The computed gain for the proposed antenna is 4.1 dBi. At 28GHz, the reflection obtained for the suggested design is -21.27db. The two-turn meander and AVL antenna are created utilizing a complete ground structure. The antenna was developed for usage with the Ka-band.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Depletion type IGFET device in Visual TCAD
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A scaling of MOSFET is difficult due to limitation of increasing in the doping concentration for semiconductor material. A high frequency and high current carrying devices are mandatory for all scaled transistors. It is required the characteristic and it’s performance should be well defined and efficient in nature. In this paper it is used to analyse the characteristics of depletion type IGFET device. The effect of doping concentration, V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gs</inf> and V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ds</inf> has been discussed with proper comparison of various combinations. Channel length modulation is doubled increasing doping concentration in the power of eight results are measured in Visual TCAD and briefly discussed. Similarly effect of V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gs</inf> in pinch off voltage and impedance are increased by increasing the gate voltage.

articleTitle: Semi-Ring Patch Array Antenna for High Gain 28 GHz Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A patch array antenna design for millimeter-wave 28 GHz applications is presented in this article. The front-side of the proposed design is comprised of a 1×2 array of semi-ring radiating elements excited using a conventional T-junction corporate feeding network, while the back-side consists of a full ground plane. The designed patch array demonstrates a wide impedance bandwidth (1.75 GHz), ranging from 27.5 GHz to 29.25 GHz. Furthermore, a peak gain of ≥9.5 dBi with an antenna efficiency of >80% is observed within the operating bandwidth.

articleTitle: Isolation Enhancement of Fractal Structure MIMO Antenna for 5G Wearable Device Applications: Design and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper proposed fractal structure MIMO antenna design for 5G wearable device applications. Jeans was employed as the substrate material, which has a dielectric constant of 1.7. The single antenna dimension is 49×55×1mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> and orthogonal fractal MIMO antenna dimension is 123 52.5×1mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. The SIMO fractal structure antenna is built after the single element rectangle shaped antenna is produced for 3.5GHz operating frequency. Using a SISO fractal structure antenna, a side by side MIMO fractal structure antenna is designed. After developing the orthogonal placement of antenna, compares the outcomes of the side by side MIMO antenna with the orthogonal MIMO antenna. A side by side MIMO antenna has a -20dB isolation, but an orthogonal MIMO antenna has a -34dB isolation. As a consequence, an orthogonal MIMO antenna's isolation is improved by -13dB. Overall, the simulation findings suggest that the orthogonal MIMO antenna provides better results, with improvements in isolation, gain, ECC and TARC. Finally, Wearable antennas are very large to be used in a current wearable on-body communication system that can be integrated into smart clothing.

articleTitle: Ultra-Thin Single Layered FSS with Closely Spaced Quad Band Response and Higher Angular Stability
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel single layered frequency selective surface (FSS) design with high angular stability and closely spaced quad band response. The unit cell of the proposed 3-D FSS design is imprinted using 0.25 mm FR-4 substrate as the base for the patch elements. The design thus proposed consists of concentric "sun like" structures encompassed inside a rectangular frame. The unit cell size is very compact having dimensions 0.028λ*0.028λ*0.003λ. The novel proposed structure resonates at frequencies. The four adjacent pass bands obtained at 4.1 GHz, 5 GHz, 6.1 GHz, and 8 GHz are separated by sharp transmission zeroes leading to desired rejection response on both sides. The novel proposed structure finds application for upcoming 5G technology which falls in the Sub Gigahertz range along with various other C band applications.

articleTitle: X-Band High Power GaN SPDT Switch MMIC for Space based Radar Front End
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents the design and realization of a X-Band GaN HEMT based high-power Single Pole Double Throw (SPDT) switch for a space based phased array RADAR front ends. The switch is designed using the space qualified 0.25um GaN-on-SiC process of United Monolithic Semiconductors. The switch is designed using series-shunt configuration and its performance is measured and evaluated over the frequency band of 9 GHz – 11 GHz. and fits in a size of 1.3mm X 1.79mm. The switch exhibits state-of-art performance with an insertion loss of less than 0.85dB, isolation> 25 dB and on-state power handling capability of better than 42 dBm at 0.5 dB insertion loss compression point. The input return loss is better than 20dB and the output return loss of both the on and off states are better than 17dB over the entire bandwidth.

articleTitle: Channel estimation of mmWave Massive MIMO System using multi cell-based Pilot allocation protocol integrated with deep neural network
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Massive MIMO has been demonstrated to be effective in 5G networks (multiple-input multiple-output) is an advanced method. Massive MIMO systems use cellular BS (Base Stations) with an abundance of antennas to distribute numerous single-antenna consumers concurrently. By considering the PC (Pilot Contamination) issue, there is a limited massive MIMO system performance. Pilot assigns massive MIMO systems randomly to all users. This paper intended the channel detection in mmWave massive MIMO system for pilot decontamination by multi cell-based pilot allocation protocol integrated with DNN. To enhance users’ uplink throughput and tackle PC issues, in multi-cell large MIMO networks the pilot allocation protocol is used. In order to protect consumers with a weak channel state from the effects of acute interference, large-scale fading channel characteristics were worn throughout the pilot allocation method. The proposed approach outperformed the pilot allocation technique using DNN, according to experimental data.The parametric analysis bides conducted by SINR of 49.9 dB, BER of 58.8%, MMSE of 57.1%, and spectral efficiency of 88.9%. Simulation results verify that combining pilot allocation with DNN can significantly improve the system.

articleTitle: Design and Real Time Application of Cost Efficient Portable Ground Station Antenna at VHF Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The present paper highlights the design and development of a double-cross dipole antenna for a low-earth orbit satellite ground station (GS) application. The proposed ground station antenna (PGSA) has a hemispherical radiation pattern (RP), so it can capture signals coming from all directions. The paramount aim of this research work is to design and fabricate a portable as well as cost effective antenna at VHF band for ground station application. It has a return loss of - 30.489 dB with a maximum gain of 5.389 dB at a resonant frequency of 137 MHz Also, the PGSA has simulated and measured impedance bandwidth (VSWR ⩽ 2) of 10.4 MHz (132.2-142.6 MHz, 7.6%) and 12.6 MHz (132-144.6 MHz, 9.2%). The signal reception of the fixed-site ground station using the PGSA has been done successfully. The receiver system can decode and display images transmitted from NOAA-19 satellite for further analysis of satellite images. The PGSA structure has been modified in such a manner that it could be folded as per the requirement and made portable to receive signal from NOAA-19 satellite for GS application.

articleTitle: Revolutionary Deployable Parabolic Reflector for Ka, W, and G-band Operation for Earth Science Mission
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A solution for wide bandwidth high frequency (up to 240GHz) deployable reflector is needed to enable a new type of low-cost and platform-versatile Earth Science missions. Deployable mesh reflectors are limited to a maximum frequency of 60GHz due to the mesh limitations (i.e. surface accuracy and reflectivity). Leveraging on a revolutionary deployable solution, the proposed antenna can operate at frequencies up to 240GHz with an overall surface root mean squared error of 31 microns. In this paper, we are assessing the feasibility of this reflector to operate at 238.5GHz. A Ka- and W-band dual-band deployable reflector is proposed achieving excellent efficiency of 69% and 63% at Ka- and W-band.

articleTitle: Design Of A Small Size 8 × 8 Butler Matrix In C-Band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents the design of 4 × 4 and 8 × 8 Butler matrices in C band at 5.8 GHz center frequency. These matrices have been designed in C band with the intention of using them in avalanche detection system in future. The topology used for designing the Butler matrices has dimensions much smaller as compared to the conventional topology and it is easy to design and fabricate as well. However, being designed at a higher frequency, the input and output ports are so close to each other that placement of connectors becomes very challenging. This paper also addresses this issue wherein, the entire network has been redesigned and rigorously optimized so that the connections can be made easily and obtained results are not disturbed much as well. The network has been designed on Rogers RT5880 (Lossy) substrate. The performance of the fabricated 4 × 4 Butler matrix has been evaluated. The experimental results shows that transmission coefficients obtained are approximately 6.7 dB across the output ports with a maximum amplitude imbalance of 0.5 dB. Isolation and Return loss obtained are below -17dB and -21 dB respectively. Maximum insertion loss obtained is 0.8 dB, whereas average insertion loss is 0.65 dB. Phase shifts at the output ports achieved are satisfactory as well. Once the 4 × 4 Butler matrix was designed successfully with desired results, it has been used for the designing of 8 × 8 Butler matrix. The simulation results obtained for 8 × 8 Butler matrix are satisfactory. The transmission coefficients obtained are approximately -10 dB with maximum amplitude imbalance of 0.7 dB. The isolation between the ports and return loss obtained are better than -16.5 dB and -17 dB. Phase shifts obtained are also satisfactory.

articleTitle: A Markov Chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) Gibbs Sampler Augmented with Zero Forcing Detection for OTFS Reception
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The Orthogonal Time Frequency Space (OTFS) is a two-dimensional modulation scheme that operates in the Delay-Doppler domain and is robust in the presence of wireless channels experiencing a high Doppler spread. The OTFS converts a fast-varying doubly-dispersive wireless channel in the time-frequecy domain to a near-static channel in the Delay-Doppler domain. The informative symbols are transmitted in this Delay-Doppler domain with the effect that the transmitted symbols experience a channel fade that changes comparatively slowly with time. In this paper, we propose an enhanced Markov Chain Monte Carlo Markov Chain (MCMC) based Gibbs sampling scheme for the detection of transmitted symbols at the OTFS receiver. A novelty of our proposal is to combine the Zero Forcing Detection (ZFD) with the MCMC-Gibbs algorithm. We show that the proposed joint Gibbs-ZFD method avoids a performance loss that the Gibbs method exhibits at a high signal to noise ratios (SNRs). We conduct a simulation-based evaluation of our proposed approach over a range of the UE (User Equipment) speeds and for Binary Phase Shift Keying (BPSK) and Quadrature Phase Shift Keying (QPSK) modulation schemes. The numerical results show that our proposal offers an improved probability of symbol detection error compared to the two alternative OTFS receivers, namely the Gibbs method and the ZFD.

articleTitle: Designing of Polarization Insensitive Microwave Absorber for WLAN Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a polarization insensitive microwave absorber designed for Wireless Local Area Network (WLAN) application. Triple conducting metallic patch designed on dual FR4 substrate. Top and bottom metallic layers are designed in such a way that radio frequency (RF) wave impinges in the dielectric surface. Third metallic layer between substrates reduces transmission. The absorption of proposed absorber verified on different incidence angle under TE and TM polarization. The result and analysis indicates that at 5.5 GHz, absorption exceeds 90%.

articleTitle: A Broadband 29 dBm GaAs pHEMT Power Amplifier with High Gain
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Design and realization of a broadband high gain 29dBm power amplifier is presented in this article. The proposed design approach utilizes a unique combination of FET stacking to enhance unit cell power output with broadband power amplification using Non-Uniform distributed topology on GaAs pHEMT technology. Addition of feedback based driving stages helps in increase of the overall small signal gain. The resulting power amplifier gives small signal gain of 31 dB over 5-18 GHz bandwidth and delivers more than 29 dBm saturated output power when operated with 8V drain supply while consuming a total current of 600 mA.

articleTitle: System Design of a High Resolution Wide Swath SAR Based on MIMO SAR Concept
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Multi Input Multi Output (MIMO) based SAR system allows to overcome the trade-off between wide swath and high azimuth resolution imaging of conventional SAR systems. This paper presents end to end system design methodology for High Resolution Wide Swath (HRWS) imaging system based on MIMO-SAR technique. In this paper we have presented, in a procedural format, the system parameter calculation for HRWS system to image 120km swath width at 2m azimuth resolution. Practical limitations in selection of different system parameters and their impact on system performance is also discussed. Feasibility for adding additional imaging modes, possible with proposed hardware are also discussed.

articleTitle: Circular Microstrip Antenna inspired by Metamaterial and U-shaped Notch for ISM Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Metamaterials have drawn the considerable attention of researchers in recent years because of their promising applications in the field of electromagnetics, especially antennas. The metamaterial-inspired structures can provide a negative index of refraction which results in the enhancement of qualitative parameters of the Antenna. In this article, the design of a circular microstrip antenna (CMSA) along with an inverted rectangular U-shaped notch in the radiating patch and a Split Ring Resonator (SRR) in the ground plane as a metamaterial structure is illustrated. The unit cell structure of SRRs is analyzed and its electromagnetic behaviour on the proposed antenna structure is elaborated. The etching of SRR unit cells into the ground plane of CMSA forms a discontinuous ground plane. The surface current lengthening with a slight reduction in resonating frequency is observed by cutting an inverted rectangular U-shaped notch in the radiating structure of CMSA. The combined effect of notching and SRR structures etched in the ground plane provides overall broadband operation. The designed microstrip line-fed CMSA resonates at a frequency of 2.45GHz and with the size 0.294λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.506λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.013λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> (where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the free-space wavelength at 2. 45GHz). The overall structure is analyzed and validated using HFSS (High Frequency Structure Simulator). The frequency is shifted slightly from 2. 46GHz to 2. 48GHz with a -10dB|S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf>|bandwidth of 60MHz(fractional bandwidth 2. 44%) and a reflection coefficient of – 23. 39dB therby showing a matched characteristic in terms of reflection coefficient and Voltage Standing Wave Ratio (VSWR). The overall gain of the antenna is just improved from 1. 5dBi to 2. 4dBi. The features of this proposed antenna design have appealing characteristics in the ISM band along with small size, low cost, and broadband operation.

articleTitle: A Slotted Octagonal Patch Antenna for Multi-Band and High Gain Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a slotted octagonal patch antenna is presented for high-gain and multiband applications. The proposed antenna dimensions are 32×34×1.6mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup>. An octagonal patch antenna incorporating two square slots offering a peak gain of 9.48dBi at 18GHz. Incorporating an octagonal slot at the center of square slots resulting a multiband with a bandwidth of 190MHz (8.69GHz to 8.88GHz), 350MHz (11.52GHz to 11.87GHz), 360MHz (14.01GHz to 14.37GHz) and 1 .99GHz (16.01-18GHz) with a peak gain of 9.89dBi at 18GHz. The simulations are done using ANSYS HFSS software.

articleTitle: A Dual-Polarization Band-Absorptive Frequency-Selective Rasorber for S-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a dual-polarized band-absorptive frequency selective rasorber (FSR) for WLAN, Bluetooth, WiMAX, and WiFi applications. The FSR provides an absorption band and a lowpass band with low insertion loss below the absorption band. The structure consists of a lossy layer cascaded with a bandstop frequency selective surface (FSS). A Jerusalem-loaded square ring embedded with lumped resistors composes the top lossy layer. The bandstop FSS is realized by combining a square ring and a cross-dipole. Full-wave simulated results show that the FSR exhibits an absorption band (S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> ≤ −10 dB, S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf> ≤ −10 dB) from 1.82-4.01 GHz (75.12%), covering the S-band with a thickness of 0.14λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</inf> at 1.82 GHz. At the same time, it is almost transparent to the incident electromagnetic waves below 0.31 GHz (|S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">21</inf>| ≥ – 1 dB, S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> ≤ −10 dB). The structure is polarization-insensitive and exhibits a stable performance for oblique incidence up to 30 deg for dual-polarization. The proposed FSR can be deployed as radomes in military communications for low-frequency antennas.

articleTitle: Wideband Vertically Polarized Magnetic Dipole Antenna for MIMO Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a mode-superposed wideband vertically polarized(VP) half-mode substrate integrated waveguide (HMSIW) antenna with a double-layered structure is proposed. The conventional HMSIW antenna can be considered as a magnetic dipole antenna. It is constructed with the help of a three-sided closed cavity and opened at one side, yielding a very low impedance bandwidth (IBW) (below 5%) for the profile below 0.038 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> (λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the free space wavelength at the centre frequency). In order to enhance the IBW of the HMSIW antenna, a double-layered structure with an air gap has been incorporated. The half-TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">110</inf> and half-TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">310</inf> are the two adjacent modes of the HMSIW. So, in this manuscript by combining these two adjacent modes by placing the two pairs of slots at the null position of half-TE<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">310</inf>, the IBW of VP magnetic dipole is further increased. The proposed structure provides 26.40% of impedance bandwidth and 3.8 dBi as a peak endfire realized gain with the dimension as 1.259λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>× 0.363λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>× 0.038λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">L</inf>. In order to design a four-port multi-input multi-output (MIMO) antenna, the proposed structure is arranged orthogonally. The proposed wideband VP MIMO antenna exhibit very good isolation, along with the MIMO parameters.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic Design of Four-Port Waveguide Rotary Switch
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This Paper presents details of the design of four-port waveguide rotary switch for high frequency RF application. Switch consists of an actuation system and a rotor with high frequency waveguide for RF transmission. In microwave communication systems, waveguide rotary switches typically operate in high frequency band applications for providing redundancy. The proposed design eliminates the need for a separate electromagnetic actuator and instead provides a compact, integrated switch mechanism with electromagnetic coil arrangement for path switching. Analysis of effects of detent and developed torque in the actuation system in low frequency regime is provided. Actuation system design is optimized based on parametric simulations. High frequency RF simulation and optimization is carried out for waveguide cavity. The RF simulation results show return loss better than 20 dB and insertion loss less than 0.2 dB. By iterative design of chokes in waveguide rotor, the port isolation is improved up to 80 dB.

articleTitle: High Spectral Purity Clock for High Speed ADC and DAC
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper describes the generation of high spectral purity clock for high speed ADC and DAC. ADC and DAC requires low jitter clock is essential to achieve high performance. 500MHz and 1000MHz clocks required for ADC and DAC respectively and also derived from high stable OCXO 125MHz reference signal by using two frequency multipliers (X2 and X4). Based on the clock requirements, an architecture and implementation finalised. Finally, the fabricated prototype was measured. The maximum sampling clock of ADC is 1.3ns and RMS jitter is 0.2ps and for ADC and DAC provides, 12-bit resolution, 3 Gsps Guaranteed Conversion Rate and master clock to DSP is 1.6ns. BPF is selected for wide stopband rejection at 1GHz and 500MHz, and LPF is utilised in the following step to offer rejection greater than 40 dB, output level to the DAC is 5dBm and for ADC is 0dBm.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Surface Wave Transmission Line Microwave Sensor for Measuring Grain Moisture Content
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a microwave sensor designed for grain moisture-content measurement using surface wave transmission line technology. The sensor utilizes a microstrip line structure to excite a surface wave, which propagates along the grain surface. The dielectric properties of the grain are affected by its moisture content, and this change in dielectric constant is used to calculate the moisture content. The sensor was tested with wheat sample and was found to have a high accuracy and precision in measuring moisture content. The design of the sensor is compact and easy to use, making it suitable for use in various grain storage and processing facilities.

articleTitle: A Compact Large-Signal Model Generation of GaN HEMT for RF Circuit Design Implication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a compact large-signal model generation of GaN HEMT using measured DC and S-parameters, has been presented. This model employs the linear and nonlinear models. The linear model is generated for bias-dependent intrinsic parameters. The non-linear capacitance model has been used, which is based on a hyperbolic function, improves the accuracy of the capacitance behavior near the pinch-off region. The Angelov current model is used as the current source model to describe the electrical (I-V) behavior of HEMT. The model has been validated with the measured DC and S-parameter results.

articleTitle: Optimizing Beam Congruence of a Solid Cassegrain Reflector and an Offset-Fed Deployable Mesh Reflector
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Two multi-beam Ku-band reflector antennas are designed for a NASA’s Earth Science mission concept. This satellite could carry two antennas: a center-fed Cassegrain fixed reflector and an offset-fed deployable mesh reflector. Each support 7 near-nadir beams at Ku-band with matched patterns between the two antennas. The feeds are arranged to achieve a desired cross-track overlap at the 1.5 dB point of the antenna pattern. This solution takes advantage of the platform motion to achieve the desired scan pattern with a simple switched-horn solution. This paper describes the design approach of the two antenas to achieve identical beam pointing and beamwidth despite using different optical prescription.

articleTitle: An Optimum Microwave Filter Design Using Groove Gap Waveguide Technology for Low-loss High-power Applications at Ku and Q-band
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents an optimum design of groove gap waveguide filter at Ku and Q-band. The row of bed of nails is varied to improve the in-band performance (insertion loss) of the filter. The concept is validated through third order Chebyshev filter designed with fractional bandwidth 1.92% at 13 GHz and 1.97% at 38GHz respectively. The filter is designed with different number of rows of nails and its performance is simulated. The high-power analysis of the filter is carried out which finds it to be a prospective candidate for high power filter application. The filter designed with groove gap waveguide technology offers the advantage of easier manufacturing compared to cavity filter, which reduces the overall cost involved in the production and makes it a suitable candidate for bulk production.

articleTitle: 8-14 GHz Ultra-wideband Negative Feedback MMIC Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper describes the design and measurement results of an ultra-wideband compact monolithic microwave amplifier. The amplifier uses a series inductor, resistor and capacitor as the feedback element, whose values are analyzed and optimized to achieve the desired response. The amplifier is designed using 150nm pseudomorphic high-electron mobility transistor process of WIN foundry and it fits in a compact size of 1.7mm x 1.5mm x 0.1mm. With DC power consumption of only 28mW, the developed amplifier features small signal gain of 10.5dB with gain response of ±1.2dB across the frequency band ranging from 8GHz to 14GHz, an output power of 9.44 dBm @10.5 GHz.

articleTitle: Designing of a Dual Band Compact Polarization Insensitive Metamaterial Absorber for X-band and Ku-band Application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In present work, the designing and simulation study of a dual band microwave metamaterials absorber has been represented. The proposed structure was designed by considering the incident direction of electromagnetic wave on the surface for electromagnetic interference (EMI)/ electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) applications. The proposed absorber unit cell consist of slots on upper surface of dual side copper coated FR-4 epoxy glass substrate of thickness 3.2 mm. The designed unit cell has dimension of 10 X 10 mm with four fold symmetry, which makes it less sensitive to polarization of incident electromagnetic wave. The proposed absorber offers two distinct absorption peak with 99.89, 99.83 FWHM bandwidth of 571 MHz (11.46 -12.04 GHz) at 11.8 GHz and 751 MHz (14.08-14.84 GHz) at 14.41 GHz respectively under normal incidence for TE and TM modes. Proposed absorber structure shows polarization independent behavior for different values of incidence angle for TE and TM modes. The designed absorber unit cell has compactness of 0.39 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.39 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> with ultra-thin thickness of 0.12 λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> is the free space wavelength, with respect to the lowest absorption peak of 11.80 GHz. Absorption mechanism of proposed unit cell has been discussed with the help of normalized input impedance, electric field distribution and surface current density plots.

articleTitle: Miniaturized SIW-based Cavity-Backed Antenna
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper comprises a single-layered Substrate Integrated Waveguide (SIW) based cavity-backed antenna used for military and WiMAX applications. The SIW is a technology that can efficiently integrate waveguide into a substrate itself. The cavity-backed antenna is constructed on a single PCB having metallic vias array shorted from top to ground conducting planes. The proposed antenna is miniaturized, planar, robust, and efficient. The performance of the antenna is investigated in terms of the S11-parameter, efficiency, and gain. The antenna miniaturization is achieved by 22.8% in both of the frequency bands. The bandwidth is achieved around 900 MHz at 4.4 GHz and 700 MHz at 5.6 GHz. The directivity of the antenna is 5.49 dBi in the lower frequency band and 4.21 dBi in the upper-frequency band while efficiency is better than 67% in both frequency bands.

articleTitle: Magic Tee Using Gap Waveguide Technology
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a gap waveguide technology-based planar magic tee component designed at W band. The proposed four-port magic tee is implemented using two different guiding structures such as ridge gap waveguide (RGW) and groove gap waveguide (GGW) transmission lines. First, the two gap waveguide transmission lines are realized at W band. Later, the performance of each structure is characterized with respect to reflection coefficient characteristics. Secondly, the H plane of the magic tee is realized using RGW structure and the E arm of magic tee is realized using GGW structure. The simulation results show reflection coefficient characteristics better than -10dB over the entire W band. In addition, the magic tee has isolation better than 30 dB between the orthogonal ports and between the collinear arms. It also achieves good amplitude and phase imbalance over the entire operating bandwidth. The proposed magic tee serves as a promising candidate in developing a comparator circuit which is a key requirement in millimeter wave monopulse tracking radar.

articleTitle: Design of 2x2 Multi-Band MIMO Antenna for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a novel 2x2 wideband multiple-input-multiple-output (MIMO) antenna is proposed. The novel design exhibits pattern diversity and displays pentaband characteristics over the multiple bands. "Pi-shaped" slot is etched on each radiating element resulting in complementary radiation patterns and improved bandwidth. Centralized staircase and "comb-like" structure is etched resulting in improved S parameters. Decoupling technique is used in the ground plane to enhance isolation among the antenna elements. The proposed MIMO antenna is designed using FR4-epoxy substrate of dimensions 0.513λ*0.292λ*0.008λ. The novel antenna thus radiates at frequencies 1.60GHz, 2.31GHz, 2.92GHz, 3.43GHz and 4.65GHz. Observed inter element isolation is more than 11 dB with a peak value of 60dB. The proposed novel design has an operational bandwidth of 4.1 GHz and can be used for multiple wireless applications.

articleTitle: 4-Port Extended Ultrawideband MIMO/Diversity Antenna for Indoor and outdoor wireless communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A compact extended ultrawideband four element MIMO antenna for indoor and outdoor wireless communication application is proposed. The antenna consists of four half hexagonal shaped monopole antenna elements. To provide polarization diversity and worthy isolation, all the antenna element are positioned orthogonally to one another. In order to verify the simulation results, a prototype of the proposed antenna has been fabricated and measured. The matching bandwidth, isolation, radiation profile, and peak gain of antennas all have been analyzed. Additionally, the analysis of MIMO performance in terms of diversity gain from S-parameter and envelop correlation coefficient (ECC) has been done. The measured impedance bandwidth of the proposed antenna is 140.42% (2.8 GHz to 16 GHz) where measured isolation is more than 15 dB, and ECC is less than 0.05.

articleTitle: A Circular Patch Antenna with Bottleneck feed and DGS for C-Band and X-Band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a circular patch antenna with bottleneck feed and DGS is proposed. The antenna is fed with a bottleneck microstrip feed. The proposed antenna is developed on an FR-4 substrate with a thickness of 1.65 mm. The proposed antenna is a dual-band antenna operating with a bandwidth of 2.98 GHz (4.62 - 7.60 GHz) and 4.34 GHz (8.68 - 13.02 GHz) with a return loss of -37.79 dB at 5.6 GHz and -31.45 dB at 10.18 GHz. The peak gains obtained are 2.55 dBi and 5.59 dBi at 5.65 GHz and 10.15 GHz respectively. The Ansys HFSS EM Solver is used to simulate the proposed antenna.

articleTitle: A High Performance Rectangular Waveguide Band Pass Filter for 5G Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents a high-performance band pass filter (BPF) realized in rectangular waveguide technology to be used in sub-6 GHz 5G communication base-station transceivers. The filter utilizes advanced state-of-the-art design methodology to achieve the stringent specifications demanded by the application. The BPF designed from 3.3 GHz to 3.7 GHz has a measured pass band insertion loss better than 0.4 dB and return loss better than 18 dB over the bandwidth. The BPF achieves a stringent rejection of 60 dB at +30 MHz offset and has a spurious free window more than 500 MHz. The measured group delay variation is within 40 ns over the entire bandwidth.

articleTitle: High Performance Antenna Feed Systems for Satellite Communications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Antenna feed systems are critical components of satellite payloads. They are used as feeds for reflectors, elements in a phased or direct radiating arrays or single radiating elements. This paper presents high performance feeds systems used for various satellite services. Key requirements, design aspects, manufacturing methods, and RF performance of feed systems at various frequency bands are discussed including applications.

articleTitle: Square patch with symmetrical L-slots resonating at 915 MHz for Hyperthermia application
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: An L-slot square patch antenna that operates at 915 MHz for a hyperthermia application is the subject of modeling experiments in this research study. In a multi-layered phantom, the simulated reflection coefficient and specific absorption rate (SAR) are investigated. The proposed antenna is 93.75x93.75x1.6 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sup> in size. At various penetration depths, the SAR is obtained for the x-axis variation inside the phantoms.

articleTitle: A Material Insensitive Photonic Band Gap Structured for Tunable THz Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: We propose a Theoretical investigation of narrow band photonic band gap structured filter of THz frequency. This analysis is based on THz frequency(~THz) which is existed in Transmission Spectrum. The photonic band gap structures influence on different materials have been analyzed and their radiation properties are discussed in this article. Using different materials, the frequency can be tuned according to usage of different materials.

articleTitle: Electrically Small Broadband CRLH Metamaterial Inspired Antenna in C-Band for 5G Laptop Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: An electrically small, broadband, cheap, simple, and efficient CRLH metamaterial transmission line inspired antenna has been designed and studied in the C-band for 5G applications. The antenna is designed on an FR-4 substrate of 1 mm thickness and is electrically connected to a 15.6-inch laptop display ground plane. The antenna studied achieves a broad -10 dB S<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">11</inf> bandwidth of 1.8 GHz (3.3 GHz – 5.1 GHz). This covers the entire C-band (N77/N78/N79) in the FR-1 range for 5G applications. The total area occupied by the miniaturized antenna is approximately $0.0283\lambda _{\text{g}}^2\left( {86.6{\text{m}}{{\text{m}}^2}} \right)$, where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">g</inf> is the wavelength on the substrate at 3.3 GHz. It exhibits relatively high total antenna efficiencies and peak realized gains including near omni-directional pattern in the azimuthal plane (plane perpendicular to the plane of the antenna structure). The simulated results show that the designed antenna is appropriate for 5G applications in laptops.

articleTitle: Investigating the Improved Microwave Absorption Bandwidth in Fe/ZnO Composite-Backed Cross-Dipole FSS: A Critical Analysis
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The performance of magneto-dielectric composites to absorb microwave energy can be significantly increased by imprinting frequency selective surface (FSS) features on them, as is well known. However, optimizing such FSS absorbers remains a challenging endeavor. In order to achieve this, a critical examination of the effects of cross-dipole FSS structural parameters on the frequency response and bandwidth performances of composite material backed FSS absorber has been undertaken in this study. This work uses the High-Frequency Structural Simulator (HFSS) numerical simulation software in 8 – 18 GHz frequency range. The impact of cross-dipole length, width, and composite material substrate thickness on the microwave absorption performance of the Fe/ZnO composite-backed cross-dipole FSS was analyzed in this study. The absorption bandwidth of the composite absorbing material layer was significantly expanded from 5.17 (11.43-16.6) GHz to 8.22 (8.64-16.86) GHz by imprinting Cross-dipole FSS with a 2.5 mm coating thickness. The proposed FSS absorber's absorption behavior has also been explained through the analysis of surface current distribution. The conclusion will aid in the design of highly efficient cross-dipole FSS microwave absorber.

articleTitle: Methodology for In-orbit testing of high throughput spot beam communication payload
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: With the time, the need for spectrum usage or the bandwidth, among users of satellite communication has increased which resulted in the development of payload in higher frequency band (Ka, Q&V band). Further the need for higher output power from the satellite for mobile internet users also arises. To facilitate these requirements into the satellite, payload with spot beam coverage has been designed. This type of the satellite which provides higher throughput of data are known as High throughput satellite. Before handing over of the payload/transponder to users, comprehensive In-orbit testing (IOT) of the payload is carried out to verify its performance after withstanding vibration and thrust by launch vehicle. This paper presents IOT setup validation and measurement philosophy for in-orbit testing of payload of trending High throughput spot beam satellite.

articleTitle: Design of Quasi Yagi Antenna with square resonator for Wireless Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, a high gain, dual-frequency band operating quasi-Yagi antenna is suggested. In order to operate on two bands, a dual band Yagi antenna is modified by the addition of two square type resonators with a slight split in one side. The antenna gain is high at both bands, and the resonators create a new resonant frequency band. The antenna is well-matched, as seen by the measured and modelled findings, which show antenna gains of 5.65 dB and 6.11 dB, respectively, at 1.90 GHz and 2.38 GHz. The suggested antenna is efficient, small, and has a high gain, making it suitable for usage in a variety of wireless communication and radio frequency energy harvesting applications.

articleTitle: Low profile, High Gain with modified Circular Shaped feed Rectangular DRA
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A microstrip feed Dielectric Resonator Antenna (DRA) with a modified circular patch is proposed. It has low profile, wideband, and high gain. The antenna is constructed with a low permittivity rectangular dielectric that is mounted on the top of the substrate. The microstrip feeding and stubs with the suitable dimensions is used to stimulate a significant coupling between the feeding element and DRA. The results show that the gain has been substantially increased and broadside radiating modes are generated by this configuration. The proposed antenna offers 42% impedance bandwidth and peak gain within the impedance bandwidth is 9.1dBi. In addition, the proposed DRA has a low profile and operates in the "X" band, and "Ku" band frequencies which is suitable for various wireless communication systems. Gain enhancing approach along with low profile and wideband for the DRA is demonstrated in this paper.

articleTitle: All-Metal Circular Polarized Patch Excited Cup Antennas for Lunar Farside Seismic Suite (FSS)
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: All metal patch circularly polarized S-band antennas are being developed at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory for the Lunar Farside Seismic Suite (FSS). The antennas are proposed to be used as a telecommunication antenna between 2.2 and 2.3 GHz. A single element and 2 × 2 elements patch excited cup antennas have been developed for wide beam circular polarization over 60° elevation angle while surviving the harsh temperature variations during the Lunar day and night. The antenna prototypes have been fabricated and tested and they fulfil the performance requirements.

articleTitle: A Printed Design of Fabry-Perot Cavity Antenna with High Gain-Bandwidth Product
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: A printed Fabry-Perot cavity antenna (FPCA) is designed to achieve high gain-bandwidth product. The proposed FPCA uses printing technology to achieve a compact, lightweight, and low-cost design with improved mass production capabilities. The primary radiator is a rectangular microstrip patch with dual-offset aperture feeding. With the help of a novel version of aperture field theory, an engineered metal-grid superstrate is realized. In this study, EM simulation and experiments are used to validate the proposed concept and theory. The measured broadside gain of the fabricated antenna prototype reaches 17.4 dBi at 10 GHz and remains above 11.5 dBi over 62.5% of the impedance bandwidth (8.2-15.6 GHz). The proposed antenna offers a 3dB gain-bandwidth product (3dB-GBP) and an average gain-bandwidth product (AGBP) of 2033 and 1992, respectively. This has never been achieved from a printed FPCA before. Over the desired bandwidth, the front-to-back ratio (FBR) remains above 35 dB.

articleTitle: Estimation of Q-factor and Its Comparison with Simulation Result for a Resonant Transmission Line having Microwave Device Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper, Q-factor of a resonant microstrip line is expressed analytically considering all types of loss from microstrip line (MTL), split ring resonator (SRR), and also, from dielectric substrate. For modeling, a lumped element equivalent circuit is assumed and then, using Lagrangian formalism, the necessary equations are developed to calculate average energy stored and power dissipation from this coupled system. For different split-gap orientations of a single gap square-shaped SRR, the Q-factors of the resonator are calculated with different coupling distances assuming the same set of geometrical parameters of this coupled system. Also, simulated Q-factors are obtained using CST Microwave Studio, and they are compared with analytical results.

articleTitle: A compact C-shaped Stub Loaded Quad-band monopole antenna for Wireless applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The proposed paper presents a compact quad-band microstrip patch monopole antenna with a tunable capability. The proposed monopole antenna is formed by introducing the three C-shaped stubs of different lengths with a rectangular ring. The antenna uses an FR-4 substrate with a thickness of 0.5 mm. The proposed antenna is fed by a 50Ω CPW line and has a compact size of 20×21 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The antenna operates at 2.58 GHz, 3.47 GHz, 3.66 GHz, and 4.07 GHz frequencies. The key parameters such as reflection coefficient, peak gain, and antenna radiation pattern are analyzed using ANSYS electronic desktop HFSS software.

articleTitle: Modal Analysis of scattering through Spheroidal Lens Antenna by Sectioning
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: In this paper scattering of the spheroidal lens antenna is analyzed by slicing the lens into odd number of sections that are spherically symmetric. The contour of each slice is closely approximated by a spherical curvature in height. The field contribution of each section is computed by symmetric and rapid application of partial spherical lens scattering. The field at any point in space is the sum of contribution of individual sections. The incident and scattered fields are directly expressed as a linear combination of spherical vector wave function of each lens section. This method is compared with results obtained from numerical computation using an EM solver (HFSS) for a Spheroidal lens (15 cm × 9 cm) excited by a 2×2 array antenna operating at 10GHz. The results are further validated satisfactorily with measured patterns in anechoic chamber.

articleTitle: Blind Digital Beamforming Techniques for Next Generation Communication Systems
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: Beamforming has become an essential technique for next-generation wireless systems. Digital beamforming is known to provide optimal beamforming performance and is robust with advanced signal processing techniques. In this paper, we focus on developing various algorithms which blindly estimate the symbols. Blind beamforming algorithms proposed for a single user do not put any constraint on the structure of the signal, unlike already existing source separation methods. For multiple users, a threshold-based Iterative Least Squares with Projection (ILSP) is proposed, an advancement to ILSP where the symbols near the decision boundary are not wrongly projected. Furthermore, when the users are located closely in the spatial domain, we present an algorithm which utilises Estimation of Signal Parameters via Rotation Invariance Technique (ESPRIT), a subspace-based method to estimate the Direction of Arrival (DoA) precisely. Consequently, the symbols are estimated using the interference cancellation technique. Finally, we develop a Neural Networks (NN) based beamforming algorithm that predicts the symbols of the user of interest.

articleTitle: A Triple Band Polarization Independent Metamaterial Absorber for S, C and X-band Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper asserts an exploration of a compact, ultrathin triple-band metamaterial absorber (MA), which is polarization insensitive. The unit cell structure proposed comprises three different resonating structures, namely structure 1, structure 2, and structure 3. The unit cell structure consists of three layers in which resonating structures are printed on top of substrate material (FR-4), which has a thickness of 1 mm. The bottom layer of dielectric material is circumscribed with a thin layer of copper. Under normal incidence, our proposed structure presents three different absorptivity peaks of 99.89%, 99.85%, and 97.82% for 3.59GHz, 6.82GHz, and 11.96GHz, which have FWHM bandwidth of 157.38MHz (3.513-3.670GHz), 304.89MHz (6.682-6.986GHz), and 629.14MHz (11.658-12.287GHz) respectively in TE mode. The proposed structure is unconstrained on polarization by its four-fold symmetricity property. Our proposed unit cell structure provides the compactness of 0.119λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> × 0.119λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, which provides a needle-like thickness of 0.011λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf>, where λ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</inf> represents the wavelength of free space regarding the lowest peak of absorptivity at 3.59GHz. The variation of MA parameters: effective input impedance, effective permittivity and effective permeability, are shown against frequency to describe the absorption procedure for the proposed unit cell structure.

articleTitle: High-Isolation Dual-band Shared Aperture Binomial Antenna Array for Airborne Synthetic Aperture Radar Applications
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: The article presents a two-bands (X/Ku) binomial antenna array with linear polarizations for a shared aperture antenna. The proposed standard linear-polarized antenna array has several advantages low cost, low profile, high isolation, and low cross-polarization. The amplitude distributions of dualdifferent bands of binomial array antenna are creatively linked in the same aperture and resonant at different frequencies. Because of the compact of high isolation and low polarized, binomial arrays are presented as X/Ku-band elements, and the size of the designed antenna was 210×60×0. 8mm3. The results are provided by using CST Microwave Studio Simulator. In this method, series feed center-fed and open stub with reduced polarization levels are simulated for two different operational frequencies (9.3GHz, and 13.265GHZ) at isolation between port-1 and 2 is -57, The bandwidth of 0.088%(X-band) and 1.79%(Ku-Band), Return Loss for 25dB/-15.7dB and Proposed antenna gains are X/KU 13.7dBi/13.4 dBi. The antenna provides high isolation and low cross-polarization above 25 dB. A proposed tapering technique for an antenna X/Ka-band linear-polarized antenna array has been described, which may be helpful in Synthetic Aperture Radar applications

articleTitle: Monopole versus Rectangular Microstrip Patch Antenna for Short Range Wireless Communication
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper presents the performance analysis of microstrip patch antenna (MSA) and a quarter wave monopole antenna (MP) intended for short range wireless communication. In this paper, the design of a co-axial feed single layer microstrip patch antenna at 2.4 GHz WLAN application is presented. This antenna design is based on Arlon AD250C substrate of 1.6 mm thickness, with a dielectric constant of ϵ<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> ≈ 2.5. To verify its response characteristics, the antenna is simulated using CST Microwave Studio. The radiation parameters of simulated, fabricated and experimental results are presented. A good match between simulated and measured quantities are obtained. The radiation pattern is directional, making it more suited for short distance point to point wireless communication, rather than a standard monopole (λ/4) whip antenna, which is commercially available for 2.4 GHz. We have also presented experimental results and tabulated various parameters for both, the patch as well as for MP antenna. We compare and contrast the best antenna suited for short range wireless communication system.

articleTitle: Studies on the Design of Ultra Wide Band Antennas for Fetus Monitoring*
publicationTitle: 2023 IEEE Wireless Antenna and Microwave Symposium (WAMS)
abstract: This paper present an array of Ultrawide-band (UWB) antenna for fetus monitoring application. The fetus of the voxel model of Katja female consisting of the five tissues namely the Uterus cervix, umbilical cord, skin, fat, and amniotic fluid are considered in the simulation model. The dielectric properties of these tissues has been studied over an UWB frequency ranges from 3.1 - 10.6 GHz. A circular patch UWB antenna is designed on a dielectric substrate FR-4 (lossy) and fed it by a 50 Ω microstrip line with maximum size of 42 mm X 50 mm. The antenna has been tested to provide an ultrawide 10 dB return loss over UWB frequency range with satisfactory radiation properties. Further, the array of UWB antenna is simulated with and without the voxel model tissues. In the simulated model we have considered one antenna as a transmitting antenna and other as receiving antennas at one point of time. The transmission coefficient of the receiving antennas are presented over the UWB frequency band. The variation of reflection, transmission coefficient, and far-field radiation pattern with and without the fetus of the voxel model demonstrate the validity of our proposed model for fetus monitoring over a period of time during the pregnancy.
